records.literal_gloss: And upon this came the disciples of him, and they were marveling that with a woman he was speaking; no one however said, "What do you seek?"

en.L: And at this [moment] {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} disciples came, and they were marveling that {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} was speaking with a woman; yet no one said, "What are {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} seeking?"
en.B: At that moment {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} disciples arrived, and they were astonished that {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} was speaking with a woman. Yet none of them said, "What are {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} looking for?"
en.R: Right then Jesus's disciples came back. They were amazed that {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} was talking with a woman. But none of them asked {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, "What do {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} want from her?"

es.L: Y en esto llegaron {{deity_pronoun:sus|Sus}} discípulos, y se maravillaban de que hablara con una mujer; sin embargo, nadie dijo: «¿Qué buscas?»

es.R: Justo entonces volvieron los discípulos de Jesús. Se sorprendieron de que hablara con una mujer. Pero ninguno {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} preguntó: «¿Qué quieres de ella?»

fr.B: À ce moment-là, {{deity_pronoun:ses|Ses}} disciples arrivèrent, et ils s’étonnèrent de {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} voir parler avec une femme. Pourtant aucun d’eux ne dit : « Que cherches-{{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} ? »
fr.R: Juste à ce moment-là, les disciples de Jésus sont revenus. Ils ont été très surpris de {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} voir parler avec une femme. Mais aucun d’eux ne {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} a demandé : « Qu’est-ce que {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} lui demandes ? »

decisions.choice: at this: just as Jesus said "I am he" (4:26)
decisions.reason: The phrase marks the moment. The disciples, who had gone into the town to buy food (4:8), come back at the very point where Jesus has told the woman who he is, and the conversation ends.

decisions.choice: they were surprised that a teacher was talking in public with a woman
alternatives: surprised only that she was a Samaritan
decisions.reason: John says "a woman", not "a Samaritan": the surprise is that a teacher was talking alone with a woman he did not know. Jewish teaching of the time was wary of this; the Mishnah, collected about AD 200, records the saying "do not talk much with a woman" (Avot 1:5). That she was also a Samaritan (4:9) made it stranger still. The imperfect verb pictures their surprise as lasting while they took in the scene.

decisions.choice: both questions are ones they might have put to Jesus, and did not
alternatives: the first question is to the woman (what do you want?), the second to Jesus
decisions.reason: The verbs are singular, and the second question, "why are you speaking with her?", is plainly to Jesus; joined by "or", the two are most naturally alternatives put to the same person. μέντοι ("yet") shows that respect for their teacher kept them quiet. "What are you seeking?" is the question Jesus himself asked the first disciples (1:38).

Every pronoun for Christ uses the deity_pronoun setting, including "you" when people speak to him, as here, even though the question is not spoken aloud. At the start of a sentence "He" is written plain. This applies throughout the passage.

decisions.choice: What are you looking for? (B); What do you want from her? (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced uses the same everyday words as at 1:38, so the echo stays visible; Readable says plainly what the question would have meant here and supplies "from her", which the scene implies.
Balanced uses the same words as at 1:38 ("¿Qué buscan?"), so the echo stays visible; Readable says plainly what the question would have meant here.

decisions.choice: narration in the passé simple (L, B), with Literal keeping John's present tense ("dit"); passé composé (R); speech in the passé composé at every level
alternatives: passé composé for narration at every level
the present tense throughout at Literal
decisions.reason: The French brief for the whole passage (4:27-54). The passé simple ("arrivèrent", "crurent") is the normal tense of written narrative and suits a public reading; Literal uses it for the Greek past tenses and keeps the present where John tells a past event in the present (4:28, 4:34, 4:49, 4:50 "dit"), as the English Literal does. Readable uses the passé composé ("les disciples sont revenus"), the past tense French readers speak and learn first. Inside speech every level uses the passé composé ("il m’a dit tout ce que j’ai fait"). The imperfect ("s’étonnaient", "priaient") is used at every level for what was going on.

English Readable says what the question would have meant here ("What do you want from her?"). The French idiom "Qu’est-ce que tu lui veux ?" sounds hostile, as if Jesus meant her harm; "Qu’est-ce que tu lui demandes ?" is plain and fits the scene, since Jesus had asked her for a drink (4:7).

decisions.choice: disciples call Jesus "Thầy", with no deity_pronoun span
decisions.reason: As the style guide sets out, the disciples address Jesus as "Thầy" (Teacher) and speak of themselves as "chúng con"; "Thầy" is a noun of address, always capitalised, so it takes no setting.

decisions.choice: no deity_pronoun spans; "그분", "께서" and the honorific "-시-" carry the respect
alternatives: a deity_pronoun span around "그분" (it would have nothing to change)
decisions.reason: Korean has no capital letters, so the deity_pronoun setting has nothing to change and the Korean text has no such spans in this passage. Respect for Jesus is carried at every level by the honorific forms.

decisions.choice: the sentence ends with a comma, and "no one said" is completed in the next sentence
alternatives: repeat the full clause "아무도 ... 묻지 않았다" in both sentences
decisions.reason: Korean puts the verb after the quotation, so "no one said" must follow the first question; the second question (its own sentence in the SBLGNT) then takes its own "하고 묻지도 않았다".

decisions.choice: no deity_pronoun spans in Amharic: pronouns for Jesus are written plainly (ደቀ መዛሙርቱ, ይናገር)
decisions.reason: The Ethiopic script has no capital letters, so the reader's setting for capitalised pronouns has nothing to change in Amharic. Pronouns for God and for Jesus are written plainly throughout this passage.

decisions.choice: ማንም ... አላለም (no one said ...) after the first question, repeated after the second (4:27b)
alternatives: one verb of saying after both questions, carried into the next record
decisions.reason: Amharic puts the verb of saying after the words quoted. Each record must read as a sentence, so this one ends with "አላለም" and the next repeats it (in brackets at Literal) after the second question.

Devanagari has no capital letters, so the deity_pronoun setting has nothing to change in Hindi. Respect for Jesus is carried by the honorific third person ("उनके", "रहे हैं") and by "आप" when people speak to him, at every level.

decisions.choice: "आप क्या ढूँढ़ते हैं?" (L); "आप क्या ढूँढ़ रहे हैं?" (B)
decisions.reason: The same verb as Jesus's question in 1:38 ("तुम क्या ढूँढ़ते हो?"), so the echo stays visible; Readable says what the question would have meant here. Literal brackets the name Hindi needs to keep the two "वे" apart.

decisions.choice: light honorifics for Jesus in narration ("話しておられる"); the disciples speak to him politely ("求めておられるのですか", "お求めですか")
decisions.reason: As the John terms settle: the narrator uses light respect forms for what Jesus does, and the disciples address their teacher in polite speech. Jesus speaks plainly with authority. This holds for the passage.
Readable says what the question would have meant here, "what do you want with her?", as the English Readable does; Literal and Balanced keep the verb "seek" (求める) that echoes 1:38.

decisions.choice: she left the jar behind as she went off to the town
alternatives: a deliberate sign that she no longer cares for well water (4:13-15)
decisions.reason: She came to draw water (4:7), and now she leaves the jar at the well, perhaps in haste and meaning to come back. Some readers see a picture in it: she has found the living water Jesus spoke of (4:10-14). John does not say so, so every level simply reports it.
The word is used of any walled or settled place, small or large. Here it is Sychar, the town near Jacob's well (4:5).

decisions.choice: the people of the town, men and women
alternatives: only the men, gathered in a public place
decisions.reason: The plural of this word is the ordinary term for people in general; it does not mark them as male. Those she speaks to are the townspeople who then come out (4:30) and of whom many believe (4:39-42).
The word means people in general (meaning decision m3), so the inclusive word is the default and the gender setting gives the traditional "men".

John often tells a story in the present tense ("she says") for vividness. Literal keeps the present; Balanced and Readable use the past, as stories are normally told in this language. This applies to every such verb in the passage.
Sychar was a small place (meaning decision m2); "city" would suggest something much larger.
Readable shows the haste implied by her leaving the jar and going at once.

decisions.choice: historic present at Literal; pretérito at Balanced and Readable
decisions.reason: As elsewhere in John: Literal keeps John's present ("llega", "le dice"); Balanced and Readable use the pretérito. This applies throughout the passage.
The word means people in general (meaning decision m3): inclusive default, traditional one tap away.
The Greek word is the one used for the stone jars of 2:6, which Spanish calls "tinajas". Here it is the jar she carried to the well, which Spanish calls a "cántaro".

French "ville" names any town, small or large, and is the plain word for a place like Sychar (meaning decision m2); "village" would make it smaller than the Greek says, and "bourgade" is literary. The same word is used through the passage (4:30, 4:39).
A cruche is the jug a woman carried to the well; "jarre" is kept for the large stone jars of 2:6.

decisions.choice: everything I have done: an overstatement that sums up her life
alternatives: a full list of her deeds
decisions.reason: Jesus had told her about her five husbands and the man she now lived with (4:16-18). That he knew this was enough to show he knew her whole life. Her words also echo what she said of the Messiah: "he will tell us all things" (4:25).

decisions.choice: a hesitant question that hopes but does not claim: could this be the Christ?
alternatives: a question expecting yes: is not this the Christ?
a question expecting no: this cannot be the Christ
decisions.reason: μήτι normally introduces a question that expects "no" (as in 4:33). Here, as in Matthew 12:23, it voices a guarded hope: she does not dare to assert it, but she raises it so that others will come and judge for themselves. The renderings keep the question tentative. Some older versions turned it into a confident "Is not this the Christ?", which the form does not support.

decisions.choice: the Christ: the title, the Anointed One she has just spoken of (4:25)
decisions.reason: With the article the word is a title. The woman herself used the Hebrew word Messiah, which John translates (4:25). Samaritans accepted only the five books of Moses, and their hope rested on the promise of a prophet like Moses (Deuteronomy 18:15-18); later Samaritan writings speak of a coming restorer who would reveal the truth.

decisions.choice: Come, see: she invites others as Philip invited Nathanael
decisions.reason: The two plural commands repeat the pattern of 1:39 and 1:46, "come and see": the one who has met Jesus brings others to see for themselves. The woman becomes the first witness to Jesus in Samaria (4:39).
A title with the article, so every level writes "the" outside the span, as at 1:20.

decisions.choice: Could this possibly be ...? (B); Might he be ...? (R)
alternatives: He cannot be the Christ, can he?
decisions.reason: These keep the hesitation of the question (meaning decision m2) without turning it into a denial or a confession.
These keep the hesitation of the question (meaning decision m2): "¿No será...?" voices a guarded hope in everyday Spanish, without turning it into a denial or a confession.
A title with the article, as at 1:20.

decisions.choice: Se pourrait-il que ... ? (L, B); Est-ce qu’il serait ... ? (R)
decisions.reason: The question hopes without claiming (meaning decision m2). French "Ne serait-ce pas ... ?" expects the answer yes and turns it into a quiet confession; "Se pourrait-il que ... ?" and the conditional "serait" keep it open.

decisions.choice: the woman addresses the townspeople in 합쇼체 ("보십시오", "제가", "저에게")
decisions.reason: She speaks to the people of the town as a group, and 합쇼체 is the polite public address; the humble "저" fits a woman of low standing speaking to them.
"혹시" with a negative question hopes for yes without claiming it, which is how the meaning decision reads the Greek; "-일 수 있겠습니까?" would sound doubtful.

alternatives: Este não pode ser o Cristo, pode?
decisions.reason: "Será que" is how Portuguese asks a hesitant question that hopes without claiming (meaning decision m2); "Não é este ...?" would turn it into a confession.
The Greek question hopes but does not claim (meaning decision m2). Amharic "ይሆን" asks just that: 'might it be?'. Amharic has no article, so "ክርስቶስ" reads as the title here at every level.

"मसीह" is both the familiar name and the word Messiah itself, so the choice the English setting offers is already made in Hindi (style guide section 7); with no article it reads as the title, as in 1:20.

decisions.choice: plain forms for the man she met ("जिसने", "यही", "वह")
decisions.reason: She speaks to her townspeople of a stranger, "a man", as people who do not yet know who Jesus is do (style guide section 7b); her question hopes but does not claim (meaning decision m2). Those who have come to believe speak of him with honorific forms (4:42).
The title she has just spoken of (verse 25). Russian has no article, so the title needs no extra word under either option.
The meaning decision: a hesitant question that hopes but does not claim.

decisions.choice: "もしや / ひょっとすると / もしかしたら……なのでしょうか"

decisions.choice: the woman says "aku" to the people of her town
decisions.reason: To her own townspeople she speaks as an equal, with "aku", where to the stranger at the well she said "saya".

decisions.choice: were urging him: kept asking him to eat
decisions.reason: The verb usually means "ask", and it can mean a request as well as a question. Here what follows is a request, and the imperfect shows them pressing it more than once.

decisions.choice: Rabbi: the respectful title for a teacher
decisions.reason: The disciples use the title John explained at 1:38. They had gone to the town for food (4:8) and now offer it to him.
The book-wide choice for John: John translates the word himself (1:38), so every level keeps it.
A bare "eat" sounds abrupt; the words give the friendly tone of the disciples' request.
As in English: a bare "come" sounds abrupt; the words give the friendly tone. "Rabí" at every level, as at 1:38.

decisions.choice: "랍비" (L); "랍비님" (B, R); the disciples speak to Jesus in 합쇼체 ("잡수십시오")
decisions.reason: As the guide sets: the title is kept, and Balanced and Readable add the honorific "-님" that a Korean address needs. "잡수시다" is the honorific of "eat".

source.text: ὁ δὲ εἶπεν αὐτοῖς· Ἐγὼ βρῶσιν ἔχω φαγεῖν ἣν ὑμεῖς οὐκ οἴδατε.

am.L: እርሱ ግን፦ «እኔ እናንተ የማታውቁት የምበላው ምግብ አለኝ» አላቸው።

id.R: Tetapi {{deity_pronoun:dia|Dia}} berkata, "Aku punya makanan yang tidak kalian kenal."

decisions.choice: emphatic I and you: I have food; you do not know it
decisions.reason: Both pronouns are written out, which Greek does for emphasis: what sustains Jesus is something the disciples know nothing of.

decisions.choice: food in a sense beyond the literal, explained in verse 34
alternatives: Jesus has been given a meal
decisions.reason: Jesus speaks of food as he spoke of water with the woman (4:10-15) and of the temple with the authorities (2:19-21): his hearers take him literally, and he then explains. The disciples misunderstand (4:33) just as the woman did.

decisions.choice: you do not know: you have no knowledge of it
decisions.reason: The verb is "know". They do not know that such food exists, nor what it is.

decisions.choice: you are not aware of (B); you do not know about (R)
decisions.reason: "Know" with "food" as its object is unnatural here; these say what it means (meaning decision m3).
English needs "not aware of", but Spanish "conocer" takes a thing as its object naturally, so every level keeps the verb (meaning decision m3).

decisions.choice: Moi, j’ai ... vous, vous ne connaissez pas (L)
alternatives: J’ai ... que vous ne connaissez pas
decisions.reason: French marks the emphatic pronouns of the Greek (meaning decision m1) with the stressed forms "moi" and "vous, vous"; Balanced and Readable leave the contrast to the sentence.

decisions.choice: Jesus to his disciples: "Ta" and "các con"
decisions.reason: The style guide's forms of address: Jesus calls his disciples "các con", as a teacher his pupils, and they call him "Thầy"; kept through the book.

decisions.choice: "あなたがた" (L, B); "あなたたち" (R)
decisions.reason: The John terms: Jesus addresses more than one person as "あなたがた" at Literal and Balanced and "あなたたち" at Readable, speaking plainly. The emphatic pronouns (meaning decision m1) are kept by stating both "わたしには" and "あなたがた".

decisions.choice: what sustains Jesus is doing the Father's will
decisions.reason: Food gives life and strength; Jesus says his life is fed by obedience. The thought is like Deuteronomy 8:3, that people do not live by bread alone. Later he says, "I have come down from heaven not to do my own will but the will of him who sent me" (6:38).

decisions.choice: the one who sent me: God the Father
decisions.reason: Jesus often describes God as "the one who sent me" (5:24, 30; 6:38-39; 7:16). It presents him as the Father's envoy, who speaks and acts for the one who sent him.

decisions.choice: complete: carry through to the end
decisions.reason: The verb means to bring something to its goal. Jesus uses it again in his prayer, "I have completed the work you gave me to do" (17:4), and from the cross he says "It is finished" (19:30), from the same root.

alternatives: that I should do ... and complete (Literal)
decisions.reason: Balanced turns the purpose clause into a plain description of what his food is.

decisions.choice: what God wants. He sent me
alternatives: the will of the one who sent me
decisions.reason: Readable names God, whom "the one who sent me" means (meaning decision m2), and splits the long phrase into short sentences.

decisions.choice: lo que Dios quiere. Él me envió
decisions.reason: As in English: Readable names God (meaning decision m2) and splits the long phrase. "Él" begins a sentence and is written plain.
In the short Readable sentence "finir son travail" could be read as Jesus's own work; "le travail qu’il m’a confié" makes clear that the work is God's (meaning decision m2).

decisions.choice: የላከኝን የእርሱን ፈቃድ (the will of him who sent me)
decisions.reason: "የላከኝን ፈቃድ" alone can be heard as 'the will that sent me'; the pronoun "የእርሱን" ties the will to the sender, as the Greek genitive does. It is grammar, not an added word, so it has no brackets.

decisions.choice: "御心" and "業" (L, B); "神が望まれること" and "仕事" (R)
decisions.reason: "御心" is the living church word for God's will and "業" for the work God gives; Readable uses everyday words and names God, as the English Readable does (meaning decision m2).

decisions.choice: a common saying, or a remark on the season: either way, "the harvest is still far off"
alternatives: a saying about the time between sowing and harvest
a time note: the scene is four months before harvest, in winter
decisions.reason: The words have the shape of a saying, and "do you not say" points to something people often said; the gap between sowing and the grain harvest was about this long. But no such saying is known from elsewhere, and the words may be a plain remark about the time of year, which would place the scene in winter, some four months before the harvest in spring. Either way the point is the same: the disciples think the harvest is still to come, and Jesus says it is here now.

source.text: ἰδοὺ λέγω ὑμῖν, ἐπάρατε τοὺς ὀφθαλμοὺς ὑμῶν καὶ θεάσασθε τὰς χώρας ὅτι λευκαί εἰσιν πρὸς θερισμόν· ἤδη ὁ θερίζων μισθὸν λαμβάνει καὶ συνάγει καρπὸν εἰς ζωὴν αἰώνιον, ἵνα ὁ σπείρων ὁμοῦ χαίρῃ καὶ ὁ θερίζων.

records.literal_gloss: Look, I say to you, lift up the eyes of you and see the fields, that white they are toward harvest. \v 36 Already the one reaping a wage receives and gathers fruit into life eternal, so that the one sowing together may rejoice and the one reaping.

en.L: Look, I say to you, lift up your eyes and see the fields, that they are white for harvest. \v 36 Already the one who reaps is receiving wages and gathering fruit for eternal life, so that the one who sows and the one who reaps may rejoice together.
en.B: Listen, I tell you: raise your eyes and look at the fields. They have turned white, ready for harvest. \v 36 Already the reaper is being paid and is gathering a crop for eternal life, so that the sower may rejoice along with the reaper.
en.R: But I tell you, look up and see the fields! The grain is ripe and ready to harvest. \v 36 Already the harvester is getting paid and is gathering a crop for eternal life. So the one who plants and the one who harvests can be glad together.

es.L: {{plural_you:Miren, yo les digo: levanten los ojos y miren|Mirad, yo os digo: levantad los ojos y mirad}} los campos, que están blancos para la siega. \v 36 Ya el que siega recibe salario y recoge fruto para vida eterna, para que el que siembra y el que siega se alegren juntos.
es.B: {{plural_you:Escuchen lo que les digo: levanten la vista y miren|Escuchad lo que os digo: levantad la vista y mirad}} los campos. Ya están blancos, listos para la cosecha. \v 36 Ya el segador está recibiendo su paga y recoge una cosecha para vida eterna, para que el que siembra se alegre junto con el que cosecha.
es.R: Pero yo {{plural_you:les digo: ¡levanten la vista y miren|os digo: ¡levantad la vista y mirad}} los campos! El grano ya está maduro y listo para la cosecha. \v 36 Ya el que cosecha está recibiendo su paga y está recogiendo una cosecha para vida eterna. Así, el que siembra y el que cosecha pueden alegrarse juntos.

fr.L: Voici, je vous dis, levez vos yeux et regardez les champs : ils sont blancs pour la moisson. \v 36 Déjà celui qui moissonne reçoit [son] salaire et recueille du fruit pour la vie éternelle, afin que celui qui sème se réjouisse en même temps que celui qui moissonne.
fr.B: Écoutez, je vous le dis : levez les yeux et regardez les champs. Ils ont blanchi, ils sont prêts pour la moisson. \v 36 Déjà le moissonneur reçoit sa paie et rassemble une récolte pour la vie éternelle, pour que le semeur se réjouisse avec le moissonneur.
fr.R: Mais je vous le dis : levez les yeux et regardez les champs ! Le blé est mûr, prêt à être récolté. \v 36 Déjà, celui qui récolte reçoit sa paie, et il rassemble une récolte pour la vie éternelle. Ainsi, celui qui sème et celui qui récolte peuvent se réjouir ensemble.

sw.L: Tazama, nawaambia, inueni macho yenu mkayaone mashamba, kwamba ni meupe kwa ajili ya mavuno. \v 36 Tayari mvunaji anapokea mshahara na kukusanya matunda kwa ajili ya uzima wa milele, ili mpandaji na mvunaji wafurahi pamoja.
sw.B: Sikilizeni, nawaambia: inueni macho mtazame mashamba. Yamekuwa meupe, tayari kwa mavuno. \v 36 Tayari mvunaji analipwa, na anakusanya mavuno kwa ajili ya uzima wa milele, ili mpandaji afurahi pamoja na mvunaji.
sw.R: Lakini nawaambia, angalieni juu mwone mashamba! Nafaka imeiva, iko tayari kuvunwa. \v 36 Tayari mvunaji analipwa, na anakusanya mavuno kwa ajili ya uzima wa milele. Kwa hiyo yule anayepanda na yule anayevuna wanaweza kufurahi pamoja.

vi.L: Này, {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} nói với các con, hãy ngước mắt lên và nhìn xem các cánh đồng, vì đã trắng để gặt. \v 36 Người gặt đã đang nhận tiền công và thu hoa lợi vào sự sống đời đời, để người gieo và người gặt cùng vui mừng.
vi.B: Hãy nghe đây, {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} nói với các con: hãy ngước mắt lên mà nhìn các cánh đồng. Lúa đã chín vàng, sẵn sàng cho mùa gặt. \v 36 Ngay bây giờ người gặt đang được trả công và đang thu hoa lợi cho sự sống đời đời, để người gieo cùng vui mừng với người gặt.
vi.R: Nhưng {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} nói với các con, hãy nhìn lên các cánh đồng kìa! Lúa đã chín, sẵn sàng để gặt. \v 36 Ngay bây giờ người gặt đang được trả công và đang thu hoạch mùa màng cho sự sống đời đời. Như vậy người gieo và người gặt đều có thể cùng nhau vui mừng.

ko.L: 보라, 내가 너희에게 말한다. 너희 눈을 들어 밭들이 희어져 추수하게 된 것을 보아라. \v 36 이미 거두는 사람이 삯을 받고, 영원한 생명에 이르는 열매를 모으고 있으니, 이는 씨 뿌리는 사람과 거두는 사람이 함께 기뻐하게 하려는 것이다.
ko.B: 잘 들어라. 내가 너희에게 말한다. 눈을 들어 밭을 바라보아라. 곡식이 희게 익어 추수할 때가 되었다. \v 36 거두는 사람은 벌써 품삯을 받고 있고, 영원한 생명에 이를 곡식을 거두어들이고 있다. 그래서 씨 뿌리는 사람도 거두는 사람과 함께 기뻐하게 된다.
ko.R: 그러나 내가 너희에게 말한다. 눈을 들어 밭을 보아라! 곡식이 다 익어서 거둘 때가 되었다. \v 36 거두는 사람은 벌써 품삯을 받고 있고, 영원한 생명을 위해 곡식을 거두고 있다. 그래서 씨를 뿌린 사람과 거두는 사람이 함께 기뻐할 수 있다.

pt.L: Eis que eu lhes digo: levantem os olhos e vejam os campos, que estão brancos para a colheita. \v 36 Já o que colhe recebe salário e ajunta fruto para a vida eterna, para que o que semeia e o que colhe se alegrem juntos.
pt.B: Prestem atenção, eu lhes digo: levantem os olhos e olhem para os campos. Eles já estão brancos, prontos para a colheita. \v 36 Aquele que colhe já está recebendo o seu pagamento e ajuntando uma colheita para a vida eterna, para que aquele que semeia se alegre junto com aquele que colhe.
pt.R: Mas eu digo a vocês: olhem em volta e vejam os campos! Os grãos estão maduros e prontos para a colheita. \v 36 Quem faz a colheita já está recebendo o seu pagamento e está juntando uma colheita para a vida eterna. Assim, quem planta e quem colhe podem ficar alegres juntos.

am.L: እነሆ እላችኋለሁ፤ ዓይኖቻችሁን አንሡ፤ እርሻዎቹም ለመከር እንደ ነጡ እዩ። \v 36 ቀድሞውኑ አጫጁ ደመወዝ ይቀበላል፤ ለዘላለም ሕይወትም ፍሬን ይሰበስባል፤ ይኸውም ዘሪውና አጫጁ በአንድነት ደስ እንዲላቸው ነው።
am.B: ስሙ፤ እላችኋለሁ፤ ዓይናችሁን አንሥታችሁ እርሻዎቹን ተመልከቱ፤ ነጥተዋል፤ ለመከርም ደርሰዋል። \v 36 ቀድሞውኑ አጫጁ ደመወዙን እየተቀበለ ነው፤ ለዘላለም ሕይወትም ፍሬ እየሰበሰበ ነው፤ ስለዚህ ዘሪው ከአጫጁ ጋር አብሮ ደስ ይለዋል።
am.R: እኔ ግን እላችኋለሁ፤ ቀና ብላችሁ እርሻዎቹን እዩ! እህሉ በስሏል፤ ለመከርም ደርሷል። \v 36 ቀድሞውኑ አጫጁ ደመወዙን እየተቀበለ ነው፤ ለዘላለም ሕይወትም ሰብል እየሰበሰበ ነው። ስለዚህ የሚዘራውና የሚያጭደው አብረው ደስ ሊላቸው ይችላሉ።

hi.L: देखो, मैं तुमसे कहता हूँ, अपनी आँखें उठाओ और खेतों को देखो, कि वे कटनी के लिए सफ़ेद हो चुके हैं। \v 36 अभी से काटनेवाला प्रतिफल पाता है और अनन्त जीवन के लिए फल इकट्ठा करता है, ताकि बोनेवाला और काटनेवाला दोनों मिलकर आनंद करें।
hi.B: सुनो, मैं तुमसे कहता हूँ: अपनी आँखें उठाकर खेतों को देखो। वे पककर सफ़ेद हो गए हैं, कटनी के लिए तैयार। \v 36 अभी से काटनेवाले को प्रतिफल मिल रहा है, और वह अनन्त जीवन के लिए फ़सल इकट्ठा कर रहा है, ताकि बोनेवाला भी काटनेवाले के साथ आनंद करे।
hi.R: पर मैं तुमसे कहता हूँ, ऊपर देखो और खेतों पर नज़र डालो! अनाज पक चुका है और काटने के लिए तैयार है। \v 36 फ़सल काटनेवाले को अभी से प्रतिफल मिल रहा है, और वह अनन्त जीवन के लिए फ़सल इकट्ठा कर रहा है। इस तरह बोनेवाला और काटनेवाला दोनों मिलकर ख़ुश हो सकते हैं।

ru.L: Вот, говорю вам: поднимите ваши глаза и посмотрите на поля, что они белы для жатвы. \v 36 Уже жнущий получает плату и собирает плод в вечную жизнь, чтобы и сеющий, и жнущий вместе радовались.
ru.B: Говорю вам: поднимите глаза и посмотрите на поля. Они побелели и готовы к жатве. \v 36 Уже жнец получает плату и собирает урожай для вечной жизни, чтобы сеятель радовался вместе со жнецом.
ru.R: А {{deity_pronoun:я|Я}} говорю вам: оглянитесь и посмотрите на поля! Зерно созрело, пора собирать урожай. \v 36 Тот, кто собирает урожай, уже получает плату и собирает урожай для вечной жизни. Так что и тот, кто сеет, и тот, кто собирает, могут радоваться вместе.

uk.L: Ось кажу вам: підніміть свої очі й погляньте на ниви, що вони білі до жнив. \v 36 Уже жнець одержує плату і збирає плід для вічного життя, щоб і сіяч, і жнець разом раділи.
uk.B: Кажу вам: підніміть очі й погляньте на поля. Вони вже побіліли, готові до жнив. \v 36 Уже жнець одержує плату і збирає врожай для вічного життя, щоб сіяч радів разом зі жнецем.
uk.R: Але кажу вам: погляньте на поля! Зерно дозріло, і його вже можна жати. \v 36 Уже той, хто жне, отримує плату і збирає врожай для вічного життя. Тож той, хто сіє, і той, хто жне, можуть радіти разом.

ja.L: 見なさい、わたしはあなたがたに言う。あなたがたの目を上げて、畑が刈り入れに向けて白くなっているのを見なさい。\v 36 すでに、刈る者は報酬を受け取り、永遠の命へと実を集めている。それは、蒔く者も刈る者も共に喜ぶためである。
ja.B: さあ、わたしは言っておく。目を上げて畑を見なさい。畑はもう白く色づいて、刈り入れを待っている。\v 36 刈り入れる者はすでに報酬を受け、永遠の命に至る実りを集めている。こうして、種を蒔く者も刈り入れる者も、共に喜ぶのである。
ja.R: しかし、わたしは言う。目を上げて、畑を見なさい。穀物は実って、もう刈り入れを待っている。\v 36 刈り入れをする人は、もう賃金をもらい、永遠の命のための実りを集めている。だから、種をまく人も刈り入れる人も、いっしょに喜べるのだ。

id.L: Lihatlah, {{deity_pronoun:aku|Aku}} berkata kepada kalian, angkatlah mata kalian dan pandanglah ladang-ladang, bahwa sudah menguning untuk dituai. \v 36 Sekarang penuai sudah menerima upah dan mengumpulkan buah untuk hidup yang kekal, supaya penabur bersukacita bersama-sama dengan penuai.
id.B: Dengarlah, {{deity_pronoun:aku|Aku}} berkata kepada kalian: lihatlah ke sekeliling dan pandanglah ladang-ladang itu. Ladang-ladang itu sudah menguning dan siap dipanen. \v 36 Sekarang pun penuai sudah menerima upahnya dan sedang mengumpulkan hasil untuk hidup kekal, supaya penabur dapat bersukacita bersama penuai.
id.R: Tetapi {{deity_pronoun:aku|Aku}} berkata kepada kalian, lihatlah ladang-ladang itu! Gandumnya sudah masak dan siap dipanen. \v 36 Sekarang pun orang yang memanen sudah dibayar dan sedang mengumpulkan hasil untuk hidup kekal. Jadi orang yang menabur dan orang yang memanen bisa bergembira bersama-sama.

decisions.choice: white: grain ripened and turned pale, ready to cut
decisions.reason: Ripe wheat and barley turn from green to pale gold. Jesus speaks of the fields, and at the same time of the Samaritans who are coming out of the town toward him (4:30): they are the harvest that is ready now.

decisions.choice: already begins the next sentence: already the reaper is being paid
alternatives: already ends the sentence before: white for harvest already
decisions.reason: The manuscripts have no punctuation, and the word can end the sentence before or begin this one. The SBLGNT punctuates it with what follows, and John often puts "already" at the head of a clause (4:51; 7:14). The other reading, "white already for harvest", is old and well known from the King James Version, so a footnote gives it. Verse 36 is printed from "Already", as the punctuation suggests, though in the verse division the word stands at the end of verse 35.

decisions.choice: the harvest of the last days: people gathered for eternal life
decisions.reason: The prophets spoke of God's final gathering as a harvest (Isaiah 27:12; Joel 3:13), and Jesus uses the image for people gathered to God (Matthew 9:37-38). Here the wage is the joy of the work, and the crop is people brought to eternal life.

decisions.choice: sower and reaper rejoice together: harvest comes straight after sowing
alternatives: no echo; only the shared joy is meant
decisions.reason: Normally sowing and reaping are months apart (verse 35), and the sower may never see the crop. Here they rejoice at the same time. Amos 9:13 pictures the age to come in the same way: the one plowing will overtake the one reaping. The link to Amos is possible but not stated.

alternatives: the life of the age to come
decisions.reason: The book-wide key term for John, kept at every level.
Literal and Balanced keep the picture of pale ripe grain; Readable says "ripe" so that young readers do not imagine snow (meaning decision m1).
The word calls attention to what follows; the style guide keeps "behold" out of modern English.

decisions.choice: is being paid / is getting paid
decisions.reason: Plain words for a worker's pay.
As in English: Literal and Balanced keep the picture of pale ripe grain; Readable says "maduro" (meaning decision m1).
The word calls attention to what follows; Balanced and Readable use everyday words.

decisions.choice: moissonner, le moissonneur, la moisson (L, B); récolter (R)
decisions.reason: "Moisson" and "moissonner" are the exact words for cutting grain and carry the biblical picture of the last harvest (meaning decision m3); young readers know "récolter" and "la récolte" better, so Readable uses them.

decisions.choice: Le blé est mûr (R); blancs (L, B)
decisions.reason: As in English, Readable says what the white colour means (meaning decision m1); "blé" is the grain French readers picture in a field.
Vietnamese sees ripe grain as golden, not white; Literal keeps the Greek colour word, the other levels say what it means.

Korean does not speak of fields "turning white" for harvest, so Balanced adds "익어" (ripened) to the colour and Readable says only that the grain is ripe. "이미" (already) is kept for verse 36, as the meaning decision reads it.
Literal and Balanced keep the picture of grain turned pale (meaning decision m1), as the English does; Readable says "maduros", as the English Readable says "ripe".

alternatives: ዋጋ (reward), the word Matthew's Amharic uses for this Greek noun
decisions.reason: The Greek noun is the word Matthew uses for a reward, which the Amharic gives as "ዋጋ". Here the picture is a harvest worker being paid, so "ደመወዝ" is the natural word. The harvest picture itself is kept at every level.
Following Matthew's convention, Literal gives the Greek word with "እነሆ"; Balanced and Readable reword it.

Matthew settled "प्रतिफल" for this Greek word, and John keeps it so the word reads the same through the Gospels; within the picture it is the harvest worker's pay, which "प्रतिफल" (what one receives for one's work) also covers. "अनन्त जीवन" stays at every level.
Literal and Balanced keep the picture of pale ripe grain (meaning decision m1), Balanced adding "पककर" (ripened); Readable says "अनाज पक चुका है", as the English says "ripe".
The convention settled in Matthew for idou: 'вот' at Literal, left out at Balanced and Readable.
Ripe grain turns pale (meaning decision). Literal and Balanced keep the colour; Readable says what it means.
The Gospels convention for *idou*: "ось" at Literal, left out at Balanced and Readable, where Ukrainian marks the emphasis by the imperative itself.
The word calls attention to what follows. Literal keeps "見なさい"; Balanced uses "さあ" because "見なさい" comes again in the same sentence ("畑を見なさい").

decisions.choice: "白くなっている / 白く色づいて" (L, B); "穀物は実って" (R)
decisions.reason: Literal and Balanced keep the picture of grain turned pale and ripe; Readable says plainly that it is ripe (meaning decision m1).
m1: ripe grain turns from green to pale gold. Indonesian speaks of ripe grain as "menguning" (turning yellow); "memutih" would not be understood of a field.

source.text: ἐν γὰρ τούτῳ ὁ λόγος ἐστὶν ἀληθινὸς ὅτι Ἄλλος ἐστὶν ὁ σπείρων καὶ ἄλλος ὁ θερίζων·

records.literal_gloss: For in this the saying is true that, "Another is the one sowing and another the one reaping."

en.L: For in this the saying is true: 'One is the one who sows, and another the one who reaps.'
en.B: For here the saying proves true: 'The sower is one person, and the reaper another.'
en.R: People say, 'One person plants and someone else harvests.' And here that saying is true.

es.L: Porque en esto es verdadero el dicho: “Uno es el que siembra, y otro el que siega”.
es.B: Pues aquí se cumple el dicho: “Uno siembra y otro cosecha”.
es.R: Hay un dicho: “Uno siembra y otro cosecha”. Y aquí ese dicho es verdad.

fr.L: Car en cela le dicton est vrai : “L’un est celui qui sème, et un autre celui qui moissonne.”
fr.B: Car ici se vérifie le dicton : “L’un sème, un autre moissonne.”
fr.R: Les gens disent : “L’un sème, et un autre récolte.” Et ici, ce dicton est vrai.

sw.L: Kwa maana katika hili msemo huu ni wa kweli: 'Mmoja ndiye anayepanda, na mwingine ndiye anayevuna.'
sw.B: Kwa maana hapa msemo ule unathibitika kuwa kweli: 'Mpandaji ni mtu mmoja, na mvunaji ni mwingine.'
sw.R: Watu husema, 'Mtu mmoja hupanda na mwingine huvuna.' Na hapa msemo huo ni kweli.

vi.L: Vì trong điều này câu nói ấy là thật: 'Người gieo là một người, người gặt là một người khác.'
vi.B: Vì ở đây câu tục ngữ ấy thật đúng: 'Người này gieo, người khác gặt.'
vi.R: Người ta thường nói: 'Người này trồng, người kia gặt.' Và ở đây câu nói ấy thật đúng.

ko.L: 이 일에서 '한 사람은 씨를 뿌리고, 다른 사람은 거둔다'는 말이 참되기 때문이다.
ko.B: 사실 여기서 '씨 뿌리는 사람 따로, 거두는 사람 따로'라는 말이 들어맞는다.
ko.R: 사람들은 '씨 뿌리는 사람이 따로 있고, 거두는 사람이 따로 있다'고 말한다. 여기서 그 말이 꼭 맞는다.

pt.L: Pois nisto o dito é verdadeiro: 'Um é o que semeia, e outro o que colhe.'
pt.B: Pois aqui o ditado se mostra verdadeiro: 'Um semeia, e outro colhe.'
pt.R: As pessoas dizem: 'Uma pessoa planta, e outra colhe.' E aqui esse ditado é verdadeiro.

am.L: በዚህ “ዘሪው አንዱ ነው፤ አጫጁም ሌላ ነው” የሚለው ቃል እውነት ነውና።
am.B: “ዘሪው አንድ ሰው ነው፤ አጫጁም ሌላ ነው” የሚለው አባባል በዚህ እውነት ሆኖ ይገኛልና።
am.R: ሰዎች “አንዱ ይዘራል፤ ሌላው ያጭዳል” ይላሉ። ይህም አባባል በዚህ እውነት ነው።

hi.L: क्योंकि इसमें यह कहावत सच है: 'एक बोता है, और दूसरा काटता है।'
hi.B: क्योंकि यहाँ यह कहावत सच साबित होती है: 'बोनेवाला कोई और है, और काटनेवाला कोई और।'
hi.R: लोग कहते हैं, 'एक व्यक्ति बोता है और कोई दूसरा काटता है।' यहाँ यह कहावत सच है।

ru.L: Ведь в этом верно слово: “Один — тот, кто сеет, и другой — тот, кто жнёт.”
ru.B: Ведь здесь оправдывается поговорка: “Один сеет, а другой жнёт.”
ru.R: Люди говорят: “Один сеет, а другой собирает урожай.” И здесь эта поговорка верна.

uk.L: Бо в цьому правдиве слово: “Один — той, хто сіє, а інший — той, хто жне.”
uk.B: Бо тут справджується приказка: “Сіяч — один, а жнець — інший.”
uk.R: Люди кажуть: “Один сіє, а хтось інший жне.” І тут ця приказка правдива.

ja.L: というのは、このことにおいて、『ある者が蒔き、別の者が刈る』ということばは真実だからである。
ja.B: まさにここで、『蒔く者と刈る者とは別の人である』ということわざが当てはまるのだ。
ja.R: 人は、『種をまく人と、刈り入れる人は別だ』と言う。ここでは、そのことわざのとおりになっているのだ。

id.L: Sebab dalam hal ini benarlah peribahasa, 'Yang seorang menabur dan yang lain menuai.'
id.B: Sebab di sini peribahasa itu terbukti benar: 'Yang satu menabur, yang lain menuai.'
id.R: Orang berkata, 'Yang satu menanam, orang lain yang memanen.' Dan di sini perkataan itu benar.

decisions.choice: the saying is true: the proverb really fits this case
alternatives: the saying is merely accurate in general
decisions.reason: The adjective means true in the sense of genuine, holding good. "In this" points to the situation Jesus has just described.

decisions.choice: a saying that usually complained of unfairness
decisions.reason: The Old Testament uses the thought as a curse or a lament: one sows and another eats the crop (Deuteronomy 28:30; Job 31:8; Micah 6:15). Here the same fact becomes a reason for shared joy (verse 36): others did the sowing, and the disciples reap.

decisions.choice: the saying first, then that it is true
alternatives: For in this the saying is true: ...
decisions.reason: Readable gives the saying before saying that it fits, which is easier to follow.
The words refer to anyone who sows or reaps; plain words for a person need no gender setting.

decisions.choice: the saying first, then that it is true
decisions.reason: As in English: easier to follow. "Uno ... otro" is general and needs no gender setting.
Here the Greek word means a saying people repeat (meaning decision m1); "la parole" would suggest God's word, and "le dicton" is the everyday French word for a popular saying.

decisions.choice: "ことばは真実" (L); "ことわざが当てはまる" (B); "ことわざのとおりになっている" (R)
decisions.reason: The saying really fits this case (meaning decision m1). Literal keeps "word" and "true"; Balanced and Readable call it a proverb and say that it fits, which is how Japanese speaks of a saying coming true.

source.text: ἐγὼ ἀπέστειλα ὑμᾶς θερίζειν ὃ οὐχ ὑμεῖς κεκοπιάκατε· ἄλλοι κεκοπιάκασιν, καὶ ὑμεῖς εἰς τὸν κόπον αὐτῶν εἰσεληλύθατε.

records.literal_gloss: I sent you to reap what not you have toiled; others have toiled, and you into the toil of them have entered.

en.L: I sent you to reap what you have not toiled over; others have toiled, and you have entered into their toil."
en.B: I sent you to reap what you did not labor over. Others did the labor, and you have taken up where their work left off."
en.R: I sent you to harvest a crop that you did not work for. Other people did the hard work before you, and now you are gathering what they worked for."

es.L: Yo {{plural_you:los|os}} envié a segar lo que {{plural_you:ustedes no han trabajado|vosotros no habéis trabajado}}; otros han trabajado, y {{plural_you:ustedes han entrado|vosotros habéis entrado}} en el trabajo de ellos».
es.B: Yo {{plural_you:los|os}} envié a cosechar lo que {{plural_you:ustedes no trabajaron|vosotros no trabajasteis}}. Otros hicieron el trabajo duro, y {{plural_you:ustedes han continuado|vosotros habéis continuado}} donde ellos lo dejaron».
es.R: Yo {{plural_you:los|os}} envié a cosechar algo por lo que {{plural_you:ustedes no trabajaron|vosotros no trabajasteis}}. Otros hicieron antes el trabajo duro, y ahora {{plural_you:ustedes recogen|vosotros recogéis}} el fruto de su esfuerzo».

fr.L: Moi, je vous ai envoyés moissonner ce pour quoi vous n’avez pas peiné ; d’autres ont peiné, et vous, vous êtes entrés dans leur peine. »
fr.B: Je vous ai envoyés moissonner ce qui ne vous a coûté aucune peine. D’autres ont fait le dur travail, et vous en avez pris la relève. »
fr.R: Je vous ai envoyés récolter ce que vous n’avez pas cultivé vous-mêmes. D’autres ont fait le travail difficile avant vous, et maintenant vous récoltez ce qu’ils ont fait pousser. »

sw.L: Mimi niliwatuma mvune kile ambacho hamkukitaabikia; wengine walitaabika, nanyi mmeingia katika taabu yao."
sw.B: Niliwatuma mvune kile ambacho hamkukifanyia kazi. Wengine walifanya kazi hiyo, nanyi mmeendeleza pale kazi yao ilipoishia."
sw.R: Niliwatuma mvune mavuno ambayo hamkuyafanyia kazi. Watu wengine walifanya kazi ngumu kabla yenu, na sasa ninyi mnakusanya kile walichokifanyia kazi."

vi.L: Ta đã sai các con đi gặt điều mà các con đã không lao nhọc; những người khác đã lao nhọc, còn các con đã bước vào công lao của họ."
vi.B: Ta đã sai các con đi gặt những gì các con không phải lao nhọc. Người khác đã lao nhọc, còn các con thì tiếp nối công khó của họ."
vi.R: Ta đã sai các con đi gặt mùa màng mà các con không phải làm vất vả. Những người khác đã làm việc cực nhọc trước các con, và bây giờ các con thu hoạch những gì họ đã làm ra."

ko.L: 내가 너희를 보내어 너희가 수고하지 않은 것을 거두게 하였다. 다른 사람들이 수고하였고, 너희는 그들의 수고에 들어갔다."
ko.B: 나는 너희가 애쓰지 않은 것을 거두라고 너희를 보냈다. 다른 사람들이 애써 일했고, 너희는 그들이 해 놓은 일을 이어받았다."
ko.R: 나는 너희를 보내어, 너희가 일하지 않은 곡식을 거두게 했다. 너희보다 먼저 다른 사람들이 힘들게 일했고, 이제 너희는 그들이 일한 열매를 거두고 있다."

pt.L: Eu os enviei para colher aquilo por que vocês não labutaram; outros labutaram, e vocês entraram na labuta deles."
pt.B: Eu os enviei para colher aquilo em que vocês não trabalharam. Outros fizeram o trabalho pesado, e vocês continuaram de onde o trabalho deles parou."
pt.R: Eu enviei vocês para colher uma plantação em que vocês não trabalharam. Outras pessoas fizeram o trabalho duro antes de vocês, e agora vocês estão colhendo aquilo por que elas trabalharam."

am.L: እኔ ያልደከማችሁበትን ልታጭዱ ላክኋችሁ፤ ሌሎች ደክመዋል፤ እናንተም በድካማቸው ገብታችኋል።»
am.B: እኔ ያልደከማችሁበትን እንድታጭዱ ላክኋችሁ። ሌሎች ደከሙበት፤ እናንተም የእነርሱን ድካም ተረክባችሁ ገባችሁ።»
am.R: እኔ ያልሠራችሁበትን ሰብል እንድታጭዱ ላክኋችሁ። ሌሎች ሰዎች ከእናንተ በፊት በብርቱ ሠርተዋል፤ አሁን እናንተ እነርሱ የደከሙበትን እየሰበሰባችሁ ነው።»

hi.L: मैंने तुम्हें वह काटने भेजा जिसके लिए तुमने परिश्रम नहीं किया; दूसरों ने परिश्रम किया है, और तुम उनके परिश्रम में प्रवेश कर चुके हो।"
hi.B: मैंने तुम्हें वह फ़सल काटने भेजा जिसके लिए तुमने मेहनत नहीं की। मेहनत दूसरों ने की, और तुम उनकी मेहनत का फल उठा रहे हो।"
hi.R: मैंने तुम्हें ऐसी फ़सल काटने भेजा जिसके लिए तुमने मेहनत नहीं की। दूसरे लोगों ने तुमसे पहले कड़ी मेहनत की, और अब तुम वह इकट्ठा कर रहे हो जिसके लिए उन्होंने मेहनत की थी।"

ru.L: Я послал вас жать то, над чем вы не трудились; другие трудились, а вы вошли в их труд.»
ru.B: Я послал вас собирать урожай там, где вы не трудились. Трудились другие, а вы пришли и продолжили их труд.»
ru.R: Я послал вас собирать урожай, над которым вы не работали. Тяжело трудились другие люди до вас, а теперь вы собираете то, ради чего трудились они.»

uk.L: Я послав вас жати те, над чим ви не трудилися; інші трудилися, а ви ввійшли в їхню працю.»
uk.B: Я послав вас жати те, над чим ви не працювали. Інші працювали, а ви продовжили там, де закінчилася їхня праця.»
uk.R: Я послав вас збирати врожай, за який ви не працювали. Інші люди тяжко працювали до вас, а тепер ви збираєте те, заради чого вони трудилися.»

ja.L: わたしは、あなたがたが労苦しなかったものを刈り入れるために、あなたがたを遣わした。ほかの者たちが労苦し、あなたがたはその人々の労苦の中に入ったのである。」
ja.B: わたしはあなたがたを遣わして、自分では骨折らなかったものを刈り入れさせた。ほかの人々が骨折って働き、あなたがたはその働きの実りを受け継いだのである。」
ja.R: わたしは、あなたたちが自分で苦労して育てたのではない作物を、刈り入れるために遣わした。ほかの人たちが先に苦労して働き、今あなたたちは、その人たちが働いて得たものを集めているのだ。」

id.L: Aku mengutus kalian untuk menuai apa yang tidak kalian usahakan; orang lain sudah bersusah payah, dan kalian masuk ke dalam hasil jerih payah mereka."
id.B: Aku mengutus kalian untuk menuai apa yang tidak kalian kerjakan. Orang lain sudah bekerja keras, dan kalian tinggal meneruskan hasil kerja mereka."
id.R: Aku mengutus kalian untuk memanen hasil yang tidak kalian kerjakan. Orang lain sudah bekerja keras sebelum kalian, dan sekarang kalian mengumpulkan hasil kerja mereka."

decisions.choice: I sent you: spoken as already done
decisions.reason: The disciples have not yet been sent out in this Gospel (17:18; 20:21). The past tense may look back to their call to follow him, or speak of their mission as already settled. The Samaritans coming out to Jesus (4:30) are the first crop they share in; later the apostles would preach in Samaria (Acts 8:4-25). The evidence does not settle which is meant.

decisions.choice: others: those who worked before the disciples, not named
alternatives: John the Baptist and the prophets before him
the woman who brought her townspeople
decisions.reason: Jesus does not say who the others are. Jesus himself has just done the work in Samaria, and the woman has brought the town to him; the prophets and John the Baptist had prepared the ground before. Every level keeps "others" without naming them.
The verb and noun speak of tiring work. The same verb describes Jesus at the well, "tired from the journey" (4:6): the toil others have done includes his own.
Literal repeats one word three times as the Greek does; Balanced keeps the sense of hard labor.
Readable shows that their work came first; the masculine plural refers to anyone, so plain "people" needs no setting.

decisions.choice: trabajar, trabajo (L); el trabajo duro (B, R)
decisions.reason: Literal repeats one word three times as the Greek does; Balanced and Readable keep the sense of hard, wearying labor (meaning decision m3).

Literal repeats one word three times, as the Greek does (meaning decision m3); "peiner" and "peine" share a root like the Greek verb and noun and keep the sense of wearying labour that "travailler" loses.
Literal repeats one word three times, as the Greek does, and "labutar", "labuta" carry the sense of tiring work (meaning decision m3); Balanced says "trabalho pesado".

decisions.choice: "労苦" three times (L); "骨折る / 骨折って働き / 働き" (B)
decisions.reason: Literal repeats one word as the Greek repeats one root; Balanced keeps the sense of hard, wearying labour (meaning decision m3) with the everyday "骨折る".

source.text: Ἐκ δὲ τῆς πόλεως ἐκείνης πολλοὶ ἐπίστευσαν εἰς αὐτὸν τῶν Σαμαριτῶν διὰ τὸν λόγον τῆς γυναικὸς μαρτυρούσης ὅτι Εἶπέν μοι πάντα ἃ ἐποίησα.

records.literal_gloss: From now the city that many believed in him of the Samaritans because of the word of the woman testifying that, "He told me all things which I did."

en.L: And from that town many of the Samaritans believed in {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} because of the word of the woman who testified, "He told me all the things that I did."
en.B: Many of the Samaritans from that town believed in {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} because of the woman's word, as she testified, "He told me everything I have done."
en.R: Many Samaritans from that town believed in {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} because of what the woman said. She told them, "He told me all the things I have ever done."

es.L: Y de aquel pueblo muchos de los samaritanos creyeron en {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} por la palabra de la mujer que daba testimonio: «Me dijo todo lo que he hecho».
es.B: Muchos de los samaritanos de aquel pueblo creyeron en {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} por la palabra de la mujer, que daba testimonio: «Me ha dicho todo lo que he hecho».
es.R: Muchos samaritanos de aquel pueblo creyeron en {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} por lo que les dijo la mujer: «Me dijo todo lo que he hecho en mi vida».

fr.L: Or, de cette ville-là, beaucoup de Samaritains crurent en {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} à cause de la parole de la femme qui rendait témoignage : « Il m’a dit tout ce que j’ai fait. »
fr.B: Beaucoup de Samaritains de cette ville crurent en {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} à cause de la parole de la femme, qui rendait ce témoignage : « Il m’a dit tout ce que j’ai fait. »
fr.R: Beaucoup de Samaritains de cette ville ont cru en {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} à cause de ce que la femme avait dit. Elle leur répétait : « Il m’a dit tout ce que j’ai fait dans ma vie ! »

sw.L: Na kutoka mji ule Wasamaria wengi walimwamini kwa sababu ya neno la yule mwanamke aliyeshuhudia, "Aliniambia mambo yote niliyoyafanya."
sw.B: Wasamaria wengi wa mji ule walimwamini kwa sababu ya neno la yule mwanamke, alipokuwa akishuhudia, "Aliniambia kila kitu nilichowahi kufanya."
sw.R: Wasamaria wengi wa mji ule walimwamini kwa sababu ya yale aliyosema yule mwanamke. Aliwaambia, "Aliniambia mambo yote niliyowahi kufanya."

vi.L: Có nhiều người Sa-ma-ri từ thành ấy đã tin vào {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} vì lời của người phụ nữ làm chứng rằng: "Người ấy đã nói với tôi mọi điều tôi đã làm."
vi.B: Nhiều người Sa-ma-ri trong thành ấy đã tin vào {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} vì lời người phụ nữ làm chứng: "Người ấy đã nói cho tôi biết mọi việc tôi đã làm."
vi.R: Nhiều người Sa-ma-ri trong thành ấy đã tin vào {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} vì những gì người phụ nữ nói. Chị ấy nói với họ: "Người ấy đã nói cho tôi biết mọi việc tôi đã từng làm."

ko.L: 그런데 그 마을의 사마리아 사람들 가운데 많은 사람이, "그분이 제가 한 모든 일을 저에게 말씀하셨습니다" 하고 증언한 그 여자의 말 때문에 그분을 믿었다.
ko.B: 그 마을의 많은 사마리아 사람들이 예수를 믿었다. "그분이 제가 한 일을 모두 말씀해 주셨습니다" 하고 증언한 그 여자의 말 때문이었다.
ko.R: 그 마을에 사는 많은 사마리아 사람들이 여자의 말을 듣고 예수를 믿었다. 여자는 그들에게 "그분이 제가 지금까지 한 일을 모두 말씀해 주셨습니다" 하고 말했다.

pt.L: E daquela cidade muitos dos samaritanos creram {{deity_pronoun:nele|Nele}} por causa da palavra da mulher que testemunhava: "Ele me disse todas as coisas que eu fiz."
pt.B: Muitos samaritanos daquela cidade creram {{deity_pronoun:nele|Nele}} por causa da palavra da mulher, que testemunhava: "Ele me disse tudo o que eu fiz."
pt.R: Muitos samaritanos daquela cidade acreditaram {{deity_pronoun:nele|Nele}} por causa do que a mulher disse. Ela contou a eles: "Ele me disse tudo o que eu já fiz na vida."

am.L: ከዚያችም ከተማ ከሳምራውያን ብዙዎች፦ «ያደረግኩትን ሁሉ ነገረኝ» ብላ ስለ መሰከረችው ሴት ቃል በእርሱ አመኑ።
am.B: «ያደረግኩትን ሁሉ ነገረኝ» ብላ ከመሰከረችው ከሴቲቱ ቃል የተነሣ ከዚያች ከተማ ብዙ ሳምራውያን በእርሱ አመኑ።
am.R: ሴቲቱ በተናገረችው ነገር ምክንያት ከዚያች ከተማ ብዙ ሳምራውያን በእርሱ አመኑ። እርሷም፦ «በሕይወቴ ያደረግኩትን ሁሉ ነገረኝ» ብላ ነግራቸው ነበር።

hi.L: और उस नगर के बहुत से सामरियों ने उस स्त्री के वचन के कारण उन पर विश्वास किया, जो गवाही देती थी, "उसने मुझे वह सब बता दिया जो मैंने किया।"
hi.B: उस नगर के बहुत से सामरियों ने उस स्त्री की बात के कारण उन पर विश्वास किया, क्योंकि उसने गवाही दी थी, "उसने मुझे मेरा किया हुआ सब कुछ बता दिया।"
hi.R: उस नगर के बहुत से सामरियों ने स्त्री की बात सुनकर यीशु पर विश्वास किया। उसने उनसे कहा था, "उसने मुझे वह सब कुछ बता दिया जो मैंने कभी किया है।"

ru.L: Из того же города многие из самаритян поверили в {{deity_pronoun:него|Него}} по слову женщины, свидетельствовавшей: «Он сказал мне всё, что я сделала.»
ru.B: Многие самаритяне из того города поверили в {{deity_pronoun:него|Него}} из-за слов женщины, которая свидетельствовала: «Он рассказал мне всё, что я сделала.»
ru.R: Многие самаритяне из того города поверили в {{deity_pronoun:него|Него}} из-за того, что сказала женщина. Она говорила им: «Он рассказал мне обо всём, что я когда-либо делала.»

uk.L: А з того міста багато хто із самарян повірив у {{deity_pronoun:нього|Нього}} через слово жінки, яка свідчила: «Він сказав мені все, що я зробила.»
uk.B: Багато самарян з того міста повірили в {{deity_pronoun:нього|Нього}} через слово жінки, яка свідчила: «Він розповів мені все, що я зробила.»
uk.R: Багато самарян з того міста повірили в {{deity_pronoun:нього|Нього}} через те, що сказала жінка. Вона говорила їм: «Він розповів мені все, що я коли-небудь зробила.»

ja.L: さて、その町のサマリア人のうち多くの者が、「あの方は、わたしがしたすべてのことをわたしに言いました」と証しした女のことばのゆえに、[イエス]を信じた。
ja.B: その町の多くのサマリア人が、「あの方は、わたしがしたことを何もかも話してくれました」と証しした女のことばによって、イエスを信じた。
ja.R: その町の多くのサマリア人が、女の人の話を聞いてイエスを信じました。女の人は、「あの方は、わたしが今までしてきたことを全部話してくれました」と証ししたのです。

id.L: Dan banyak orang Samaria dari kota itu percaya kepada-{{deity_pronoun:nya|Nya}} karena perkataan perempuan itu, yang bersaksi, "Dia mengatakan kepadaku segala sesuatu yang telah kuperbuat."
id.B: Banyak orang Samaria dari kota itu percaya kepada-{{deity_pronoun:nya|Nya}} karena perkataan perempuan itu, yang bersaksi, "Dia mengatakan kepadaku segala sesuatu yang telah kulakukan."
id.R: Banyak orang Samaria dari kota itu percaya kepada-{{deity_pronoun:nya|Nya}} karena apa yang dikatakan perempuan itu. Dia berkata kepada mereka, "Dia memberi tahu aku semua yang pernah kulakukan."

decisions.choice: believed in him: put their trust in Jesus
decisions.reason: "Believe in" with a person is John's phrase for trusting the person (2:11). They came to trust Jesus because of what she said, the way the Gospel expects later readers to believe through others' testimony (17:20; 20:31).
John uses this verb for John the Baptist's witness to Jesus (1:7, 15, 32-34). The woman becomes a witness in the same way.

decisions.choice: the woman's word, set against Jesus's own word (4:41)
decisions.reason: John contrasts the word of the woman with the word of Jesus himself, which leads many more to believe (4:41-42). Her testimony brings them to him; his word makes their belief their own.
The Samaritans who believed were men and women, and the word "Samaritans" already includes both, so no setting is needed.
Keeps the repeated word that sets her word against his (meaning decision m3); Readable says "what the woman said" and "what Jesus said" to keep the same contrast.

decisions.choice: la palabra de la mujer (L, B); lo que les dijo la mujer (R)
decisions.reason: Keeps the contrast with Jesus's own word in verse 41 (meaning decision m3); Readable says "lo que ... dijo" in both places.
Korean "믿다" with the object particle already means trusting a person, so the construction with "into" needs nothing more, and the key term stays the verb "믿다".
Style section 6: Literal and Balanced keep "crer em" for the key term; Readable says "acreditar em", the everyday verb, where the English Readable says "believe", here and through the passage.

John's key terms keep one Amharic verb each through the book: "ማመን" for believe, with "በ-" for 'believe in', and "መመስከር" for testify. Readable says the woman 'told them', as the English Readable does.

decisions.choice: "विश्वास करना" at every level; "वचन" (L), "बात" (B, R) for her word and his (4:41)
decisions.reason: Believe is a key term in John, kept as the verb at every level (docs/john-terms.md). Each level uses one word for the woman's word here and for Jesus's word in 4:41, so the contrast of meaning decision m3 stays visible.

Literal and Balanced use "ことば" here and for Jesus's own word in 4:41, so that her word and his are set side by side (meaning decision m3); Readable says "話" and "話されたこと" to keep the same contrast in plain words.
The conventional name for the people of Samaria; it includes men and women, so no setting is needed.

source.text: ὡς οὖν ἦλθον πρὸς αὐτὸν οἱ Σαμαρῖται, ἠρώτων αὐτὸν μεῖναι παρ’ αὐτοῖς· καὶ ἔμεινεν ἐκεῖ δύο ἡμέρας.

records.literal_gloss: When therefore came to him the Samaritans, they were asking him to stay with them; and he stayed there two days.

en.L: So when the Samaritans came to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, they were asking {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} to stay with them; and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} stayed there two days.
en.B: When the Samaritans reached {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, they kept asking {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} to stay with them, and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} stayed there for two days.
en.R: The Samaritans came to Jesus and asked {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} again and again to stay with them. So {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} stayed there for two days.

es.L: Así que, cuando los samaritanos vinieron a {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}}, {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} rogaban que se quedara con ellos; y se quedó allí dos días.
es.B: Cuando los samaritanos llegaron adonde estaba, {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} insistieron en que se quedara con ellos, y se quedó allí dos días.
es.R: Los samaritanos fueron a ver a Jesús y {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} pidieron una y otra vez que se quedara con ellos. Así que se quedó allí dos días.

fr.L: Lors donc que les Samaritains vinrent à {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}}, ils {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} priaient de rester auprès d’eux ; et {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} resta là deux jours.
fr.B: Quand les Samaritains arrivèrent auprès de {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}}, ils {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} prièrent avec insistance de rester chez eux, et {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} y resta deux jours.
fr.R: Les Samaritains sont venus voir Jésus et ils {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} ont demandé plusieurs fois de rester avec eux. Alors {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} est resté là deux jours.

sw.L: Basi Wasamaria walipofika {{deity_pronoun:kwake|Kwake}}, walikuwa wakimwomba akae pamoja nao; {{deity_pronoun:naye|Naye}} akakaa huko siku mbili.
sw.B: Wasamaria walipomfikia, waliendelea kumwomba akae nao, {{deity_pronoun:naye|Naye}} akakaa huko kwa siku mbili.
sw.R: Wasamaria walimjia Yesu, wakamwomba tena na tena akae nao. Basi akakaa huko kwa siku mbili.

vi.L: Vậy khi những người Sa-ma-ri đến cùng {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}, họ nài xin {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} ở lại với họ; và {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} ở lại đó hai ngày.
vi.B: Khi người Sa-ma-ri đến gặp {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}, họ cứ nài xin {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} ở lại với họ, và {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} ở lại đó hai ngày.
vi.R: Người Sa-ma-ri đến gặp Đức Giê-xu và nài nỉ {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} nhiều lần, xin {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} ở lại với họ. Vậy {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} ở lại đó hai ngày.

ko.L: 그래서 사마리아 사람들이 그분께 왔을 때, 자기들과 함께 머물러 달라고 그분께 청하였다. 그래서 그분은 거기서 이틀을 머무셨다.
ko.B: 사마리아 사람들은 예수께 와서 자기들과 함께 머물러 달라고 거듭 청했다. 그래서 예수께서는 거기서 이틀 동안 머무르셨다.
ko.R: 사마리아 사람들은 예수께 와서 자기들과 함께 머물러 달라고 여러 번 부탁했다. 그래서 예수께서는 거기서 이틀 동안 머무르셨다.

pt.L: Então, quando os samaritanos chegaram até {{deity_pronoun:ele|Ele}}, {{deity_pronoun:lhe|Lhe}} pediam que ficasse com eles; e {{deity_pronoun:ele|Ele}} ficou ali dois dias.
pt.B: Quando os samaritanos chegaram até {{deity_pronoun:ele|Ele}}, insistiram com {{deity_pronoun:ele|Ele}} para que ficasse com eles, e {{deity_pronoun:ele|Ele}} ficou ali dois dias.
pt.R: Os samaritanos foram até Jesus e pediram a {{deity_pronoun:ele|Ele}}, várias vezes, que ficasse com eles. Então {{deity_pronoun:ele|Ele}} ficou ali dois dias.

am.L: ስለዚህ ሳምራውያን ወደ እርሱ በመጡ ጊዜ ከእነርሱ ጋር እንዲቆይ ይለምኑት ነበር፤ በዚያም ሁለት ቀን ቆየ።
am.B: ሳምራውያንም ወደ እርሱ በደረሱ ጊዜ ከእነርሱ ጋር እንዲቆይ አጥብቀው ለመኑት፤ እርሱም በዚያ ሁለት ቀን ቆየ።
am.R: ሳምራውያኑ ወደ ኢየሱስ መጥተው ከእነርሱ ጋር እንዲቆይ ደጋግመው ለመኑት። ስለዚህ በዚያ ሁለት ቀን ቆየ።

hi.L: इसलिए जब सामरी उनके पास आए, तो उनसे विनती करने लगे कि वे उनके यहाँ ठहरें; और वे वहाँ दो दिन ठहरे।
hi.B: जब सामरी उनके पास पहुँचे, तो वे उनसे बार-बार विनती करने लगे कि वे उनके साथ ठहरें, और वे वहाँ दो दिन ठहरे।
hi.R: सामरी लोग यीशु के पास आए और बार-बार उनसे विनती करने लगे कि वे उनके साथ ठहरें। इसलिए यीशु वहाँ दो दिन ठहरे।

ru.L: Итак, когда пришли к {{deity_pronoun:нему|Нему}} самаритяне, они просили {{deity_pronoun:его|Его}} остаться у них; и {{deity_pronoun:он|Он}} остался там два дня.
ru.B: Когда самаритяне пришли к {{deity_pronoun:нему|Нему}}, они стали упрашивать {{deity_pronoun:его|Его}} остаться у них, и {{deity_pronoun:он|Он}} остался там на два дня.
ru.R: Самаритяне пришли к Иисусу и всё просили {{deity_pronoun:его|Его}} остаться у них. И {{deity_pronoun:он|Он}} остался там на два дня.

uk.L: Тож коли самаряни прийшли до {{deity_pronoun:нього|Нього}}, вони просили {{deity_pronoun:його|Його}} перебути в них; і {{deity_pronoun:він|Він}} перебув там два дні.
uk.B: Коли самаряни прийшли до {{deity_pronoun:нього|Нього}}, вони почали просити {{deity_pronoun:його|Його}} перебути в них, і {{deity_pronoun:він|Він}} перебув там два дні.
uk.R: Самаряни прийшли до Ісуса і знову й знову просили {{deity_pronoun:його|Його}} залишитися з ними. Тож {{deity_pronoun:він|Він}} залишився там на два дні.

ja.L: それで、サマリア人たちは[イエスの]もとに来ると、自分たちのところに泊まってくださるようにと[イエスに]願っていた。そして[イエスは]そこに二日間泊まられた。
ja.B: サマリア人たちはイエスのもとに来ると、自分たちのところに泊まってくださいと、しきりに願った。そこでイエスは、二日間そこに泊まられた。
ja.R: サマリア人たちはイエスのところに来て、自分たちの町に泊まってくださいと何度もお願いしました。そこでイエスは、二日間そこに泊まられました。

id.L: Jadi ketika orang-orang Samaria itu datang kepada-{{deity_pronoun:nya|Nya}}, mereka meminta {{deity_pronoun:dia|Dia}} untuk tinggal bersama mereka; dan {{deity_pronoun:dia|Dia}} tinggal di sana dua hari.
id.B: Ketika orang-orang Samaria itu sampai kepada-{{deity_pronoun:nya|Nya}}, mereka terus meminta {{deity_pronoun:dia|Dia}} tinggal bersama mereka, dan {{deity_pronoun:dia|Dia}} tinggal di sana dua hari.
id.R: Orang-orang Samaria itu datang kepada Yesus dan berulang-ulang meminta {{deity_pronoun:dia|Dia}} tinggal bersama mereka. Jadi {{deity_pronoun:dia|Dia}} tinggal di sana dua hari.

decisions.choice: a Jew staying as a guest of Samaritans
decisions.reason: Jews and Samaritans did not usually share things (4:9). Here Samaritans invite a Jewish teacher into their homes, and he accepts, eating and lodging with them.

decisions.choice: stay: lodge with them, with the deeper sense of remaining
decisions.reason: The verb is the ordinary one for staying as a guest, as at 1:38-39, and here it is meant plainly. It is the same verb Jesus later uses for remaining in him (15:4-10).
The book-wide choice for John: the natural word in its ordinary sense.

decisions.choice: kept asking (B); asked again and again (R)
decisions.reason: Shows the repeated request of the imperfect verb.
The ordinary word for staying as a guest, the same as at 1:38-39 (meaning decision m2).
The French brief keeps "demeurer" for the theological sense of remaining in Jesus; here the plain sense of staying as a guest comes first (meaning decision m2), and "rester" is the natural word.
"ở lại" is also the book's word for "remain" (menō), so the ordinary stay here keeps the link the meaning decision notes.
In its ordinary sense of lodging with someone, John's verb 'remain' is the everyday "ቆየ"; the words for remaining in the theological sense are kept for passages such as 15:4-10.
The verb has its ordinary sense of lodging here, so Hindi uses "ठहरना", as in 1:38-39; "बने रहना" is kept for the theological sense.
The book-wide choice for John's 'remain': the natural word in its ordinary sense, here staying as a guest; the meaning decision notes the deeper sense.
The ordinary sense of *menō* (lodge with them), but the meaning decision notes the deeper sense of remaining; Literal and Balanced keep the verb family used for John's "remain", as in 1:38-39.

The John terms keep "とどまる" for the theological sense of the verb and use the ordinary word in ordinary senses. Here it is lodging as guests (meaning decision m2), and the same word is used for the request and for what Jesus did, as the Greek repeats one verb.

source.text: καὶ πολλῷ πλείους ἐπίστευσαν διὰ τὸν λόγον αὐτοῦ, τῇ τε γυναικὶ ἔλεγον ὅτι Οὐκέτι διὰ τὴν σὴν λαλιὰν πιστεύομεν· αὐτοὶ γὰρ ἀκηκόαμεν, καὶ οἴδαμεν ὅτι οὗτός ἐστιν ἀληθῶς ὁ σωτὴρ τοῦ κόσμου.

records.literal_gloss: And by much more believed because of the word of him, \v 42 and to the woman they were saying that, "No longer because of your speech do we believe; for ourselves we have heard, and we know that this one is truly the Savior of the world."

en.L: And many more believed because of {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} word, \v 42 and they were saying to the woman, "No longer because of your talk do we believe, for we ourselves have heard, and we know that this [one] is truly the Savior of the world."
en.B: Because of {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} own word many more came to believe. \v 42 They said to the woman, "It is no longer your report that makes us believe. We have listened to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} ourselves, and we know that {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} is indeed the Savior of the world."
en.R: Many more people believed because of what Jesus said. \v 42 They told the woman, "At first we believed because of what you told us. But now we believe because we have heard {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} for ourselves. We know that {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} really is the Savior of the world, the one who saves people everywhere."

es.L: Y muchos más creyeron por {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} palabra, \v 42 y decían a la mujer: «Ya no creemos por lo que tú dijiste, porque nosotros mismos hemos oído, y sabemos que este es verdaderamente el Salvador del mundo».
es.B: Y por {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} propia palabra muchos más llegaron a creer. \v 42 Le decían a la mujer: «Ya no creemos por lo que tú nos contaste. Nosotros mismos {{deity_pronoun:lo|Lo}} hemos escuchado, y sabemos que {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} es de verdad el Salvador del mundo».
es.R: Muchos más creyeron por lo que Jesús decía. \v 42 Le dijeron a la mujer: «Al principio creímos por lo que tú nos contaste. Pero ahora creemos porque nosotros mismos {{deity_pronoun:lo|Lo}} hemos oído. Sabemos que {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} es de verdad el Salvador del mundo, el que salva a la gente de todas partes».

fr.L: Et bien plus nombreux furent ceux qui crurent à cause de {{deity_pronoun:sa|Sa}} parole, \v 42 et ils disaient à la femme : « Ce n’est plus à cause de tes propos que nous croyons ; car nous avons nous-mêmes entendu, et nous savons que celui-ci est vraiment le Sauveur du monde. »
fr.B: Ils furent bien plus nombreux encore à croire à cause de {{deity_pronoun:sa|Sa}} propre parole. \v 42 Ils disaient à la femme : « Si nous croyons, ce n’est plus à cause de ce que tu nous as raconté. Nous {{deity_pronoun:l’|L’}}avons écouté nous-mêmes, et nous savons qu’{{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} est vraiment le Sauveur du monde. »
fr.R: Beaucoup d’autres ont cru à cause de ce que Jésus disait. \v 42 Ils ont dit à la femme : « Au début, nous avons cru à cause de ce que tu nous as raconté. Mais maintenant, nous croyons parce que nous {{deity_pronoun:l’|L’}}avons entendu nous-mêmes. Nous savons qu’{{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} est vraiment le Sauveur du monde, celui qui sauve les gens de partout. »

sw.L: Na watu wengi zaidi sana waliamini kwa sababu ya neno {{deity_pronoun:lake|Lake}}, \v 42 wakawa wanamwambia yule mwanamke, "Hatuamini tena kwa sababu ya habari uliyotupa, kwa maana sisi wenyewe tumesikia, nasi tunajua kwamba huyu kwa kweli ni Mwokozi wa ulimwengu."
sw.B: Kwa sababu ya neno {{deity_pronoun:lake|Lake}} mwenyewe watu wengi zaidi wakaamini. \v 42 Wakamwambia yule mwanamke, "Sasa hatuamini kwa sababu ya habari yako. Tumemsikiliza sisi wenyewe, nasi tunajua kwamba {{deity_pronoun:yeye|Yeye}} hakika ni Mwokozi wa ulimwengu."
sw.R: Watu wengi zaidi waliamini kwa sababu ya yale aliyosema Yesu. \v 42 Wakamwambia yule mwanamke, "Mwanzoni tuliamini kwa sababu ya yale uliyotuambia. Lakini sasa tunaamini kwa sababu tumemsikia sisi wenyewe. Tunajua kwamba {{deity_pronoun:yeye|Yeye}} kweli ni Mwokozi wa ulimwengu, yule anayeokoa watu wa kila mahali."

vi.L: Và có nhiều người hơn nữa đã tin vì lời của {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}, \v 42 và họ nói với người phụ nữ: "Chúng tôi tin không còn vì lời chị nói nữa, vì chính chúng tôi đã nghe, và chúng tôi biết rằng [Đấng] này thật là Cứu Chúa của thế gian."
vi.B: Nhờ chính lời {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}, nhiều người khác nữa đã tin. \v 42 Họ nói với người phụ nữ: "Bây giờ chúng tôi tin không phải vì lời chị kể nữa. Chính chúng tôi đã nghe {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}, và chúng tôi biết {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} thật là Cứu Chúa của thế gian."
vi.R: Còn nhiều người khác nữa đã tin vì những gì Đức Giê-xu nói. \v 42 Họ nói với người phụ nữ: "Lúc đầu chúng tôi tin vì những gì chị kể. Nhưng bây giờ chúng tôi tin vì chính chúng tôi đã nghe {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}. Chúng tôi biết {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} thật là Cứu Chúa của thế gian, Đấng cứu người ta ở khắp mọi nơi."

ko.L: 그리고 그분의 말씀 때문에 훨씬 더 많은 사람이 믿었다. \v 42 그들은 그 여자에게 말하였다. "우리가 믿는 것은 이제 더 이상 네 말 때문이 아니다. 우리가 직접 들었고, 이분이 참으로 세상의 구원자이심을 알기 때문이다."
ko.B: 예수의 말씀 때문에 훨씬 더 많은 사람이 믿게 되었다. \v 42 그들은 그 여자에게 말했다. "이제는 네 말 때문에 믿는 것이 아니다. 우리가 직접 그분의 말씀을 들었고, 그분이 참으로 세상의 구원자이심을 알게 되었다."
ko.R: 예수의 말씀을 듣고 더 많은 사람이 믿었다. \v 42 그들이 여자에게 말했다. "처음에는 네가 해 준 말 때문에 믿었다. 그러나 이제는 우리가 직접 그분의 말씀을 들었기 때문에 믿는다. 우리는 그분이 정말로 세상의 구원자이시라는 것을 안다. 그분은 모든 곳의 사람들을 구원하시는 분이다."

pt.L: E muitos mais creram por causa da {{deity_pronoun:sua|Sua}} palavra, \v 42 e diziam à mulher: "Já não é por causa da sua conversa que cremos, pois nós mesmos ouvimos, e sabemos que este é verdadeiramente o Salvador do mundo."
pt.B: Por causa da própria palavra {{deity_pronoun:dele|Dele}}, muitos mais passaram a crer. \v 42 Eles disseram à mulher: "Já não é por causa do que você contou que cremos. Nós mesmos {{deity_pronoun:o|O}} ouvimos e sabemos que {{deity_pronoun:ele|Ele}} é de fato o Salvador do mundo."
pt.R: Muitas outras pessoas acreditaram por causa do que Jesus disse. \v 42 Elas disseram à mulher: "No começo nós acreditamos por causa do que você nos contou. Mas agora acreditamos porque nós mesmos {{deity_pronoun:o|O}} ouvimos. Sabemos que {{deity_pronoun:ele|Ele}} é mesmo o Salvador do mundo, aquele que salva as pessoas de todo lugar."

am.L: በቃሉም ምክንያት እጅግ ብዙዎች አመኑ፤ \v 42 ሴቲቱንም፦ «ከእንግዲህ ወዲህ የምናምነው ስለ ንግግርሽ አይደለም፤ እኛ ራሳችን ሰምተናልና፤ ይህም በእውነት የዓለም አዳኝ እንደ ሆነ እናውቃለን» ይሏት ነበር።
am.B: ከቃሉም የተነሣ እጅግ ብዙ ሰዎች አመኑ። \v 42 ሴቲቱንም እንዲህ አሏት፦ «አሁን የምናምነው አንቺ ስለ ነገርሽን አይደለም፤ እኛ ራሳችን ሰምተነዋል፤ እርሱም በእርግጥ የዓለም አዳኝ እንደ ሆነ እናውቃለን።»
am.R: ኢየሱስ በተናገረው ነገር ምክንያት ብዙ ተጨማሪ ሰዎች አመኑ። \v 42 ሴቲቱንም እንዲህ አሏት፦ «መጀመሪያ ያመንነው አንቺ በነገርሽን ነገር ነበር። አሁን ግን የምናምነው እኛ ራሳችን ስለ ሰማነው ነው። እርሱ በእርግጥ የዓለም አዳኝ፣ በየትም ቦታ ያሉትን ሰዎች የሚያድን እንደ ሆነ እናውቃለን።»

hi.L: और उनके वचन के कारण और भी बहुत से लोगों ने विश्वास किया, \v 42 और वे उस स्त्री से कहते थे, "अब हम तुम्हारे कहने के कारण विश्वास नहीं करते; क्योंकि हमने आप ही सुन लिया है, और जानते हैं कि यही सचमुच संसार के उद्धारकर्ता हैं।"
hi.B: उनकी अपनी बात सुनकर और भी बहुत से लोगों ने विश्वास किया। \v 42 उन्होंने उस स्त्री से कहा, "अब हम केवल तुम्हारी बताई बात के कारण विश्वास नहीं करते। हमने स्वयं उनकी बात सुनी है, और हम जानते हैं कि वे सचमुच संसार के उद्धारकर्ता हैं।"
hi.R: यीशु की बात सुनकर और भी बहुत से लोगों ने विश्वास किया। \v 42 उन्होंने स्त्री से कहा, "पहले हमने तुम्हारी बात सुनकर विश्वास किया था। पर अब हम इसलिए विश्वास करते हैं कि हमने ख़ुद उनकी बात सुनी है। हम जानते हैं कि वे सचमुच संसार के उद्धारकर्ता हैं, जो हर जगह के लोगों का उद्धार करते हैं।"

ru.L: И гораздо больше поверили из-за {{deity_pronoun:его|Его}} слова, \v 42 и говорили женщине: «Уже не из-за твоих речей мы верим, ведь мы сами слышали и знаем, что этот поистине Спаситель мира.»
ru.B: Благодаря {{deity_pronoun:его|Его}} собственному слову поверили ещё многие. \v 42 Они говорили женщине: «Теперь мы верим уже не из-за твоего рассказа. Мы сами слушали {{deity_pronoun:его|Его}} и знаем, что {{deity_pronoun:он|Он}} действительно Спаситель мира.»
ru.R: Ещё больше людей поверили из-за того, что сказал Иисус. \v 42 Они говорили женщине: «Сначала мы поверили из-за того, что ты нам рассказала. А теперь мы верим, потому что сами слышали {{deity_pronoun:его|Его}}. Мы знаем, что {{deity_pronoun:он|Он}} на самом деле Спаситель мира, тот, кто спасает людей повсюду.»

uk.L: І набагато більше повірило через {{deity_pronoun:його|Його}} слово, \v 42 і жінці казали: «Уже не через твою мову віримо, бо ми самі почули і знаємо, що цей справді Спаситель світу.»
uk.B: Через {{deity_pronoun:його|Його}} власне слово повірило набагато більше людей. \v 42 Вони казали жінці: «Ми віримо вже не через твою розповідь. Ми самі слухали {{deity_pronoun:його|Його}} і знаємо, що {{deity_pronoun:він|Він}} справді Спаситель світу.»
uk.R: Ще багато людей повірили через те, що сказав Ісус. \v 42 Вони казали жінці: «Спочатку ми повірили через те, що ти нам розповіла. Але тепер ми віримо, бо самі почули {{deity_pronoun:його|Його}}. Ми знаємо, що {{deity_pronoun:він|Він}} справді Спаситель світу, той, хто рятує людей усюди.»

ja.L: そして、[イエスの]ことばのゆえに、さらにはるかに多くの人々が信じた。\v 42 そして彼らは女に言っていた。「もはや、あなたの話のゆえに、わたしたちは信じているのではない。わたしたち自身が聞いて、この方が本当に世の救い主であると知っているからだ。」
ja.B: そして、イエスご自身のことばを聞いて、さらに多くの人々が信じた。\v 42 彼らは女に言った。「わたしたちが信じるのは、もうあなたの話によるのではない。自分たちで直接聞いて、この方が本当に世の救い主であると知ったのだ。」
ja.R: イエスご自身が話されたことを聞いて、もっと多くの人たちが信じました。\v 42 その人たちは女の人に言いました。「初めは、あなたから聞いた話で信じた。でも今は、自分たちであの方の話を聞いたから信じているのだ。あの方こそ本当に、この世の救い主、すべての人を救う方だとわかった。」

id.L: Dan jauh lebih banyak lagi yang percaya karena perkataan-{{deity_pronoun:nya|Nya}}, \v 42 dan mereka berkata kepada perempuan itu, "Kami percaya bukan lagi karena apa yang kaukatakan; sebab kami sendiri telah mendengar, dan kami tahu bahwa {{deity_pronoun:dia|Dia}} inilah benar-benar Juruselamat dunia."
id.B: Karena perkataan-{{deity_pronoun:nya|Nya}} sendiri, lebih banyak lagi orang menjadi percaya. \v 42 Mereka berkata kepada perempuan itu, "Sekarang kami percaya bukan lagi karena ceritamu. Kami sudah mendengar {{deity_pronoun:dia|Dia}} sendiri, dan kami tahu bahwa {{deity_pronoun:dia|Dia}}lah sungguh-sungguh Juruselamat dunia."
id.R: Lebih banyak lagi orang percaya karena apa yang dikatakan Yesus. \v 42 Mereka berkata kepada perempuan itu, "Mula-mula kami percaya karena apa yang kamu ceritakan. Tetapi sekarang kami percaya karena sudah mendengar {{deity_pronoun:dia|Dia}} sendiri. Kami tahu bahwa {{deity_pronoun:dia|Dia}} benar-benar Juruselamat dunia, yang menyelamatkan orang di mana-mana."

decisions.choice: many more: a much larger number
decisions.reason: The phrase is "more by much", a comparison of number: many more Samaritans came to believe than the first group.

decisions.choice: your talk: what she had told them
decisions.reason: λαλιὰν means speech or what someone says, and it can mean mere talk. Set beside the "word" of Jesus it is the lesser thing, but they are not scorning her: her report brought them to him (4:39). Now they believe on firsthand hearing.

decisions.choice: they have heard for themselves and know
decisions.reason: Their belief no longer rests on another's report but on Jesus's own word. Both verbs are perfects: what they have heard and know stays with them.

decisions.choice: the Savior: a title for God himself, here given to Jesus
alternatives: a deliverer in a general sense
decisions.reason: In the Old Testament God is Israel's Savior (Isaiah 43:3, 11; 45:15, 21). In the Roman world rulers, the emperors among them, were also hailed as saviors. Only here in John's Gospel is Jesus called Savior; 1 John 4:14 says, "the Father has sent the Son as Savior of the world".

decisions.choice: the world: humanity as a whole, Samaritans as well as Jews
decisions.reason: Key term. Here κόσμου means all people. Jesus told the woman that salvation is from the Jews (4:22); Samaritans now confess that it is for the whole world (compare 1:29; 3:16-17).

alternatives: the Christ, the Savior of the world (many later manuscripts)
decisions.reason: Many later manuscripts add "the Christ" before "the Savior", as the King James Version reflects. The older manuscripts do not have it. A footnote gives it; a reviewer should check this against the apparatus.

decisions.choice: At first we believed because of what you told us. But now
alternatives: We no longer believe because of your words
decisions.reason: "No longer" implies that they had first believed on her word; Readable says so in two plain sentences.

decisions.choice: the one who saves people everywhere
decisions.reason: Readable keeps the title and adds what it means here (meaning decisions m4 and m5).
"This one" is Jesus; Balanced and Readable use the pronoun with the deity_pronoun setting.
As in English: "ya no" implies that they had first believed on her word; Readable says so.

decisions.choice: el que salva a la gente de todas partes
decisions.reason: As in English: Readable keeps the title and adds what it means here (meaning decisions m4 and m5).
"This one" is Jesus; Balanced and Readable use the stressed pronoun with the setting.
"Cứu Chúa" is the established Protestant title and keeps the sense that the title belongs to God; "Đấng Cứu Thế" already contains "the world" and would double it.
"구원자" says plainly "the one who saves" and is understood by new readers; "구주" is the familiar church word and "구세주" is common in everyday speech. A reviewer may prefer either.

decisions.choice: the townspeople speak to the woman in 해라체 ("네 말", "-이 아니다")
decisions.reason: They are her neighbours speaking among equals, which the guide sets as 해라체.
"Conversa" is the lesser word set against Jesus's "palavra" (meaning decision m2) without the scorn of "falatório".

alternatives: መድኃኒት (the church word, as in መድኃኔ ዓለም)
decisions.reason: "አዳኝ", 'one who saves', is the plain modern word and is understood by every reader. "መድኃኒት" is the old church title, but in everyday Amharic it means 'medicine'.

decisions.choice: honorific forms from the believing Samaritans ("यही ... उद्धारकर्ता हैं")
decisions.reason: Those who have come to believe speak of Jesus with respect, unlike the woman's first hesitant "this man" (4:29). "सचमुच" renders the Greek "truly", as in Luke, kept apart from the amen sayings; "उद्धारकर्ता" is the Savior.
The Luke convention keeps 'поистине' for alēthōs at Literal; Balanced and Readable use everyday words.

decisions.choice: "世の救い主" (L, B); "この世の救い主、すべての人を救う方" (R)
decisions.reason: "救い主" is the plain Japanese for Savior; "世" is the John key term (L, B), with "この世" at Readable, which also says what the title means here (meaning decisions m4, m5), as the English Readable does.

decisions.choice: plain speech ("信じているのではない", "知ったのだ") from the townspeople to the woman
decisions.reason: Neighbours speaking to one of their own speak plainly; the polite forms of 4:29 belong to her appeal to them.

source.text: Μετὰ δὲ τὰς δύο ἡμέρας ἐξῆλθεν ἐκεῖθεν εἰς τὴν Γαλιλαίαν·

records.literal_gloss: After now the two days he went out from there into the Galilee;

en.L: And after the two days {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} went out from there into Galilee.
en.B: After the two days {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} left there for Galilee.
