decisions.choice: his own homeland: left open, as the text leaves it
alternatives: Galilee, his home region (Nazareth): he goes there knowing he will not be truly honored
Judea and Jerusalem: he leaves because he was not honored there
decisions.reason: Matthew 13:57, Mark 6:4 and Luke 4:24 use the saying of Nazareth in Galilee, and John calls Jesus a Galilean (1:46; 7:41, 52). But verse 45 says the Galileans welcomed him, which is hard to fit with a saying meant to explain why he went there. On one view his homeland is Galilee, and their welcome is not real honor, since it rests on the signs they saw (2:23-25; 4:48). On another it is Judea, with Jerusalem, the city of David from whose line the Messiah came (7:42); he "came to his own, and his own did not receive him" (1:11), so he left it. The evidence is balanced, and every level keeps "his own homeland" without naming it.

decisions.choice: Jesus himself had said it: a comment by the narrator
decisions.reason: "For" introduces John's explanation of the journey. "Himself" stresses that the saying was Jesus's own. The past tense looks back to something Jesus had said, not to a word spoken at this point.

decisions.choice: homeland: the land or town of one's family
decisions.reason: The word can mean a home town or a native country, which is why the question in m1 arises.
Shows that John is recalling a saying (meaning decision m2).

decisions.choice: his own homeland, with no gender setting
decisions.reason: The proverb pictures a prophet like those of Israel, and here it is applied to Jesus; it is kept as it stands.
"Su tierra" can mean a home town or a native country, as the Greek word can, so it leaves the question of meaning decision m1 open.
The current word, as in 4:19; "선지자" is the older Protestant term.
Portuguese marks the emphatic "himself" with "o próprio", an adjective, so there is no pronoun to carry the deity_pronoun span the English "himself" has.

Prophet is "भविष्यद्वक्ता" in Literal and Balanced and the everyday "नबी" in Readable (style guide section 6), as in the parallel sayings of Matthew 13:57 and Luke 4:24; noted once for this passage. "उसके" has no gender setting, as in the English.
The past progressive form shows that John is recalling something Jesus had said (meaning decision m2); Literal keeps "証しされた" for the verb of testifying.

hi.L: तब जब वे गलील में आए, तो गलीलियों ने उनका स्वागत किया, क्योंकि जो कुछ उन्होंने यरूशलेम में पर्व के समय किया था, वह सब वे देख चुके थे; क्योंकि वे भी पर्व में गए थे।
hi.B: जब वे गलील पहुँचे, तो गलील के लोगों ने उनका स्वागत किया। उन्होंने वह सब देखा था जो यीशु ने यरूशलेम में पर्व के समय किया था, क्योंकि वे भी पर्व में गए थे।
hi.R: जब यीशु गलील पहुँचे, तो वहाँ के लोगों ने उनका स्वागत किया। वे भी फ़सह के त्योहार के लिए यरूशलेम गए थे, और उन्होंने वे सब काम देखे थे जो यीशु ने वहाँ किए थे।

ru.L: Когда же {{deity_pronoun:он|Он}} пришёл в Галилею, галилеяне приняли {{deity_pronoun:его|Его}}, видев всё, что {{deity_pronoun:он|Он}} сделал в Иерусалиме на празднике; ведь и они сами ходили на праздник.
ru.B: Когда {{deity_pronoun:он|Он}} пришёл в Галилею, галилеяне радушно приняли {{deity_pronoun:его|Его}}. Они видели всё, что {{deity_pronoun:он|Он}} сделал в Иерусалиме во время праздника, потому что и сами были там на празднике.
ru.R: Когда Иисус пришёл в Галилею, люди там радушно приняли {{deity_pronoun:его|Его}}. Они тоже ходили в Иерусалим на праздник Пасхи и видели всё, что {{deity_pronoun:он|Он}} там делал.

uk.L: Тож коли {{deity_pronoun:він|Він}} прийшов до Галилеї, галилеяни прийняли {{deity_pronoun:його|Його}}, бачивши все, що {{deity_pronoun:він|Він}} зробив у Єрусалимі на свято, бо й самі ходили на свято.
uk.B: Тож коли {{deity_pronoun:він|Він}} прибув до Галилеї, галилеяни радо {{deity_pronoun:його|Його}} прийняли. Вони бачили все, що {{deity_pronoun:він|Він}} зробив у Єрусалимі під час свята, бо й самі там були на святі.
uk.R: Коли Ісус прибув до Галилеї, тамтешні люди радо {{deity_pronoun:його|Його}} прийняли. Вони теж ходили до Єрусалима на свято Пасхи і бачили все, що {{deity_pronoun:він|Він}} там робив.

ja.L: それで、[イエスが]ガリラヤに来られたとき、ガリラヤの人々は[イエスを]迎え入れた。祭りの時にエルサレムで[イエスが]なさったことをすべて見ていたからである。彼ら自身も祭りに行っていたのである。
ja.B: ガリラヤに着かれると、ガリラヤの人々はイエスを歓迎した。彼らも祭りに行っていたので、イエスが祭りの間にエルサレムでなさったことを、すべて見ていたのである。
ja.R: イエスがガリラヤに着かれると、そこの人たちはイエスを喜んで迎えました。その人たちも、エルサレムの過越祭に行っていて、イエスがそこでなさったことを全部見ていたのです。

id.L: Jadi ketika {{deity_pronoun:dia|Dia}} sampai di Galilea, orang-orang Galilea menyambut {{deity_pronoun:dia|Dia}}, karena mereka telah melihat segala sesuatu yang dilakukan-{{deity_pronoun:nya|Nya}} di Yerusalem pada hari raya itu, sebab mereka sendiri juga datang ke hari raya itu.
id.B: Jadi ketika {{deity_pronoun:dia|Dia}} tiba di Galilea, orang-orang Galilea menyambut {{deity_pronoun:dia|Dia}}. Mereka telah melihat semua yang dilakukan-{{deity_pronoun:nya|Nya}} di Yerusalem pada hari raya itu, karena mereka juga datang ke sana untuk merayakannya.
id.R: Ketika Yesus sampai di Galilea, orang-orang di sana menyambut {{deity_pronoun:dia|Dia}}. Mereka juga sudah pergi ke Yerusalem untuk hari raya Paskah, dan mereka sudah melihat semua yang dilakukan-{{deity_pronoun:nya|Nya}} di sana.

decisions.reason: Galilean pilgrims went up to Jerusalem for the festivals (Luke 2:41-44). At that Passover Jesus cleared the temple courts and did signs that led many to believe (2:23).

decisions.choice: a welcome based on what they had seen
alternatives: a welcome that shows full faith
decisions.reason: Their welcome rests on the signs they saw. John has already said that Jesus did not entrust himself to belief of that kind (2:23-25), and his words in verse 48 point the same way. This bears on the saying in verse 44.
Readable names the feast meant (meaning decision m1).

decisions.choice: the journey first, then what they saw
alternatives: having seen ..., for they too had gone
decisions.reason: Readable puts the events in the order they happened.
As in English: Readable names the feast meant (meaning decision m1).

source.text: Ἦλθεν οὖν πάλιν εἰς τὴν Κανὰ τῆς Γαλιλαίας, ὅπου ἐποίησεν τὸ ὕδωρ οἶνον.

records.literal_gloss: He came therefore again to the Cana of the Galilee, where he made the water wine.

en.L: Then {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} came again to Cana of Galilee, where {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} had made the water [into] wine.
en.B: So {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} went back to Cana in Galilee, the place where {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} had changed the water into wine.
en.R: Jesus went back to Cana in Galilee. This was the town where {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} had changed water into wine.

es.L: Vino, pues, otra vez a Caná de Galilea, donde hizo del agua vino.
es.B: Volvió, pues, a Caná de Galilea, donde había convertido el agua en vino.
es.R: Jesús volvió a Caná de Galilea. Era el pueblo donde había convertido el agua en vino.

fr.L: Puis {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} vint de nouveau à Cana de Galilée, où {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} avait fait de l’eau du vin.
fr.B: Alors {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} retourna à Cana, en Galilée, là où {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} avait changé l’eau en vin.
fr.R: Jésus est retourné à Cana, en Galilée. C’est dans ce village qu’{{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} avait changé de l’eau en vin.

sw.L: Basi akaja tena Kana ya Galilaya, mahali alipoyafanya maji [kuwa] divai.
sw.B: Basi alirudi Kana ya Galilaya, mahali alipoyageuza maji kuwa divai.
sw.R: Yesu alirudi Kana ya Galilaya. Huo ndio mji ambapo aliyageuza maji kuwa divai.

vi.L: Vậy {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} lại đến Ca-na thuộc Ga-li-lê, nơi {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} đã làm nước [thành] rượu.
vi.B: Vậy {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} trở lại Ca-na thuộc Ga-li-lê, là nơi {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} đã biến nước thành rượu.
vi.R: Đức Giê-xu trở lại Ca-na ở Ga-li-lê. Đó là nơi {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} đã biến nước thành rượu.

ko.L: 그래서 그분은 물을 포도주로 만드셨던 갈릴리 가나에 다시 오셨다.
ko.B: 예수께서는 다시 갈릴리 가나로 가셨다. 그곳은 예수께서 물을 포도주로 바꾸신 곳이다.
ko.R: 예수께서는 다시 갈릴리에 있는 가나 마을로 가셨다. 그곳은 예수께서 전에 물을 포도주로 바꾸신 곳이었다.

pt.L: Então {{deity_pronoun:ele|Ele}} veio de novo a Caná da Galileia, onde {{deity_pronoun:ele|Ele}} tinha feito da água vinho.
pt.B: Assim, {{deity_pronoun:ele|Ele}} voltou a Caná da Galileia, o lugar onde {{deity_pronoun:ele|Ele}} tinha transformado a água em vinho.
pt.R: Jesus voltou a Caná da Galileia. Era a cidade onde {{deity_pronoun:ele|Ele}} tinha transformado água em vinho.

am.L: ስለዚህ ውኃውን የወይን ጠጅ ወዳደረገባት ወደ ገሊላዋ ቃና እንደገና መጣ።
am.B: ስለዚህ ውኃውን የወይን ጠጅ ወዳደረገባት ስፍራ፣ ወደ ገሊላዋ ቃና፣ ተመለሰ።
am.R: ኢየሱስ በገሊላ ወዳለችው ወደ ቃና ተመለሰ። ይህች ከተማ ውኃውን ወደ ወይን ጠጅ የለወጠባት ናት።

hi.L: तब वे फिर गलील के काना में आए, जहाँ उन्होंने पानी को दाखरस बनाया था।
hi.B: तब वे फिर गलील के काना में गए, जहाँ उन्होंने पानी को दाखरस में बदल दिया था।
hi.R: यीशु फिर गलील के काना में गए। यह वही जगह थी जहाँ उन्होंने पानी को दाखरस में बदला था।

ru.L: Итак, {{deity_pronoun:он|Он}} снова пришёл в Кану Галилейскую, где сделал воду вином.
ru.B: И {{deity_pronoun:он|Он}} снова пришёл в Кану Галилейскую, где когда-то превратил воду в вино.
ru.R: Иисус снова пришёл в Кану Галилейскую. Это было то самое место, где {{deity_pronoun:он|Он}} превратил воду в вино.

uk.L: Тож {{deity_pronoun:він|Він}} прийшов знову в Кану Галилейську, де зробив воду вином.
uk.B: Тож {{deity_pronoun:він|Він}} знову прийшов до Кани Галилейської, де колись перетворив воду на вино.
uk.R: Ісус повернувся до Кани в Галилеї. Це було те містечко, де {{deity_pronoun:він|Він}} перетворив воду на вино.

ja.L: それで、[イエスは]再びガリラヤのカナに来られた。そこは[イエスが]水をぶどう酒にされた所である。
ja.B: こうしてイエスは、再びガリラヤのカナに行かれた。水をぶどう酒に変えられた所である。
ja.R: イエスは、またガリラヤのカナに行かれました。そこは、前にイエスが水をぶどう酒に変えられた町です。

id.L: Lalu {{deity_pronoun:dia|Dia}} datang lagi ke Kana di Galilea, tempat {{deity_pronoun:dia|Dia}} membuat air menjadi anggur.
id.B: Lalu {{deity_pronoun:dia|Dia}} kembali ke Kana di Galilea, tempat {{deity_pronoun:dia|Dia}} dulu mengubah air menjadi anggur.
id.R: Yesus kembali ke Kana di Galilea. Di kota itulah {{deity_pronoun:dia|Dia}} dulu mengubah air menjadi anggur.

decisions.choice: a reminder of the first sign at Cana (2:1-11)
decisions.reason: John points back to the first sign so that readers connect the two. The second sign also happens from Cana (4:54), and the two stories have much in common: a request, an answer that seems to hold back, trust in Jesus's word, and belief as the result (2:5, 11; 4:50, 53).
Natural wording for the event of 2:9.

source.text: καὶ ἦν τις βασιλικὸς οὗ ὁ υἱὸς ἠσθένει ἐν Καφαρναούμ.

records.literal_gloss: And there was a certain royal official whose the son was sick in Capernaum.

en.L: And there was a certain royal official whose son was sick in Capernaum.
en.B: There was a royal official whose son lay ill at Capernaum.
en.R: In the town of Capernaum there was an official of the king who ruled Galilee. His son was sick.

es.L: Y había cierto funcionario real cuyo hijo estaba enfermo en Capernaúm.
es.B: Había un funcionario real cuyo hijo estaba enfermo en Capernaúm.
es.R: En el pueblo de Capernaúm había un funcionario del rey que gobernaba Galilea. Su hijo estaba enfermo.

fr.L: Et il y avait un certain officier royal dont le fils était malade à Capharnaüm.
fr.B: Il y avait un officier royal dont le fils était malade à Capharnaüm.
fr.R: Dans la ville de Capharnaüm, il y avait un officier au service du roi qui gouvernait la Galilée. Son fils était malade.

sw.L: Na palikuwa na afisa mmoja wa mfalme ambaye mwanawe alikuwa mgonjwa huko Kapernaumu.
sw.B: Kulikuwa na afisa mmoja wa mfalme ambaye mwanawe alikuwa mgonjwa huko Kapernaumu.
sw.R: Katika mji wa Kapernaumu kulikuwa na afisa wa mfalme aliyetawala Galilaya. Mwanawe alikuwa mgonjwa.

vi.L: Và có một quan chức của vua, con trai ông bị bệnh tại Ca-bê-na-um.
vi.B: Có một viên quan của nhà vua có con trai đang bị bệnh ở Ca-bê-na-um.
vi.R: Ở thành Ca-bê-na-um có một viên quan làm việc cho nhà vua cai trị Ga-li-lê. Con trai ông bị bệnh.

ko.L: 그리고 가버나움에 어떤 왕의 신하가 있었는데, 그의 아들이 병들어 있었다.
ko.B: 그런데 가버나움에 왕의 신하 한 사람이 있었는데, 그의 아들이 앓아누워 있었다.
ko.R: 가버나움 마을에는 갈릴리를 다스리는 왕을 섬기는 신하가 있었다. 그의 아들이 아팠다.

pt.L: E havia um certo oficial real cujo filho estava doente em Cafarnaum.
pt.B: Havia ali um oficial do rei cujo filho estava doente em Cafarnaum.
pt.R: Na cidade de Cafarnaum havia um oficial do rei que governava a Galileia. O filho dele estava doente.

am.L: በቅፍርናሆምም ልጁ የታመመበት አንድ የንጉሥ ሹም ነበረ።
am.B: በቅፍርናሆም ልጁ የታመመበት አንድ የንጉሥ ሹም ነበረ።
am.R: በቅፍርናሆም ከተማ ገሊላን የሚገዛው ንጉሥ ባለ ሥልጣን የሆነ አንድ ሰው ነበረ። ልጁም ታሞ ነበር።

hi.L: और कफ़रनहूम में राजा का एक अधिकारी था, जिसका पुत्र बीमार था।
hi.B: कफ़रनहूम में एक राजकीय अधिकारी था, जिसका पुत्र बीमार पड़ा था।
hi.R: कफ़रनहूम नगर में गलील पर राज करनेवाले राजा का एक अधिकारी रहता था। उसका बेटा बीमार था।

ru.L: И был некий царский чиновник, сын которого болел в Капернауме.
ru.B: Там был один царский чиновник, у которого в Капернауме болел сын.
ru.R: В городе Капернауме жил чиновник царя, который правил Галилеей. Его сын был болен.

uk.L: І був один царський урядовець, син якого хворів у Капернаумі.
uk.B: Був там один царський урядовець, син якого лежав хворий у Капернаумі.
uk.R: У містечку Капернаум жив урядовець царя, який правив Галилеєю. Його син був хворий.

ja.L: そして、ある王の役人がいて、その息子がカファルナウムで病気であった。
ja.B: さて、カファルナウムに、息子が病気で伏せっている王の役人がいた。
ja.R: カファルナウムの町に、ガリラヤを治める王に仕える役人がいました。その人の息子は病気でした。

id.L: Dan ada seorang pegawai istana yang anaknya sakit di Kapernaum.
id.B: Di Kapernaum ada seorang pegawai istana yang anaknya sedang sakit.
id.R: Di kota Kapernaum ada seorang pegawai raja yang memerintah Galilea. Anaknya sedang sakit.

decisions.choice: a royal official: most likely an officer of Herod Antipas
alternatives: a member of the royal family
decisions.reason: βασιλικὸς means someone belonging to the king, in his service. In Galilee the ruler was Herod Antipas (4 BC to AD 39); his title was tetrarch, but people called him king (Mark 6:14). The official could have been Jewish or Gentile; John does not say. Matthew 8:5-13 and Luke 7:1-10 tell of a centurion at Capernaum whose servant Jesus healed from a distance; John's account differs in its details, and whether it is the same event is not settled.

decisions.choice: Capernaum: a town on the Sea of Galilee, a long walk from Cana
decisions.reason: Capernaum lay on the north shore of the lake, far below Cana in the hills (compare 2:12), about 15 to 20 miles away; the exact site of Cana is not certain. Jesus's word reaches the boy without his going there.

decisions.choice: an official of the king who ruled Galilee
decisions.reason: Readable says what "royal" means here (meaning decision m1) without naming Herod, which the text does not do.

decisions.choice: the place first, then the son's illness
decisions.reason: Readable sets the scene in two short sentences.

decisions.choice: un funcionario del rey que gobernaba Galilea
decisions.reason: As in English: Readable says what "royal" means here without naming Herod (meaning decision m1).

decisions.choice: un officier royal (L, B); un officier au service du roi (R)
decisions.reason: "Fonctionnaire" now suggests a modern civil servant; "officier royal" names a man in the king's service, civil or military, which is what the Greek leaves open (meaning decision m1).

decisions.choice: "왕의 신하" (L, B); "갈릴리를 다스리는 왕을 섬기는 신하" (R)
decisions.reason: "왕의 신하" names a man in the king's service plainly; "고관" (high official) says more about his rank than the Greek does.

decisions.choice: um oficial real (L); um oficial do rei (B, R)
decisions.reason: "Oficial" is a man in the king's service, as the word means (meaning decision m1); "nobre" claims a rank the text does not give.

alternatives: የቤተ መንግሥት ሰው (a man of the court)
decisions.reason: "ሹም" is a man appointed to office, which fits an officer in the service of a king; Readable says plainly whose official he was, as the English does.
The meaning decision: most likely an officer of Herod Antipas. 'Царедворец' suggests a courtier at a palace; 'царский чиновник' says plainly that he served the king.

decisions.choice: "王の役人" (L, B); "ガリラヤを治める王に仕える役人" (R)
decisions.reason: The word names an officer in a king's service, most likely Herod Antipas (meaning decision m1). "王の役人" says that plainly; Readable explains which king without naming him, as the English Readable does. This form is used for him through 4:54.

decisions.choice: "pegawai istana" (L, B); "pegawai raja yang memerintah Galilea" (R)
decisions.reason: m1: a man in the king's service, most likely an officer of Herod Antipas. "pegawai" is the glossary word for a king's official (Terms, section 5); "istana" says whose service he is in.

source.text: οὗτος ἀκούσας ὅτι Ἰησοῦς ἥκει ἐκ τῆς Ἰουδαίας εἰς τὴν Γαλιλαίαν ἀπῆλθεν πρὸς αὐτὸν καὶ ἠρώτα ἵνα καταβῇ καὶ ἰάσηται αὐτοῦ τὸν υἱόν, ἤμελλεν γὰρ ἀποθνῄσκειν.

records.literal_gloss: This one, having heard that Jesus has come out of the Judea into the Galilee, went away to him and was asking that he would come down and heal his the son, he was about for to die.

en.L: This [man], having heard that Jesus had come from Judea into Galilee, went away to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} and was asking that {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} would come down and heal his son, for he was about to die.
en.B: Hearing that Jesus had arrived in Galilee from Judea, he went to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} and kept pleading with {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} to come down and heal his son, because the boy was dying.
en.R: He heard that Jesus had come back from Judea to Galilee. So he went to Jesus and begged {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} to come down to Capernaum and make his son well. His son was about to die.

es.L: Este, al oír que Jesús había llegado de Judea a Galilea, fue a {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} y {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} rogaba que bajara y sanara a su hijo, porque estaba a punto de morir.
es.B: Al enterarse de que Jesús había llegado de Judea a Galilea, fue a verlo y {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} suplicaba que bajara a sanar a su hijo, porque el muchacho se estaba muriendo.
es.R: Oyó que Jesús había vuelto de Judea a Galilea. Entonces fue a verlo y {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} rogó que bajara a Capernaúm a curar a su hijo, porque su hijo estaba a punto de morir.

fr.L: Celui-ci, ayant appris que Jésus était venu de Judée en Galilée, s’en alla vers {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} et {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} priait de descendre et de guérir son fils, car il allait mourir.
fr.B: Quand il apprit que Jésus était arrivé de Judée en Galilée, il alla {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} trouver et {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} supplia de descendre guérir son fils, car l’enfant était mourant.
fr.R: Il a appris que Jésus était revenu de Judée en Galilée. Alors il est allé voir Jésus et il {{deity_pronoun:l’|L’}}a supplié de descendre à Capharnaüm pour guérir son fils. Son fils allait bientôt mourir.

sw.L: Huyu, aliposikia kwamba Yesu amekuja kutoka Uyahudi hadi Galilaya, alimwendea, akawa anamwomba ashuke na kumponya mwanawe, kwa maana alikuwa karibu kufa.
sw.B: Aliposikia kwamba Yesu amefika Galilaya kutoka Uyahudi, alimwendea, akaendelea kumsihi ashuke amponye mwanawe, kwa sababu kijana alikuwa anakaribia kufa.
sw.R: Alisikia kwamba Yesu amerudi kutoka Uyahudi hadi Galilaya. Basi alikwenda kwa Yesu, akamwomba sana ashuke Kapernaumu amponye mwanawe. Mwanawe alikuwa karibu kufa.

vi.L: Người này, khi nghe rằng Đức Giê-xu đã từ Giu-đê đến Ga-li-lê, thì đi đến cùng {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} và nài xin {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} xuống chữa lành con trai mình, vì nó sắp chết.
vi.B: Nghe tin Đức Giê-xu đã từ Giu-đê về Ga-li-lê, ông đến gặp {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} và cứ nài xin {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} xuống chữa lành cho con trai mình, vì đứa bé sắp chết.
vi.R: Ông nghe tin Đức Giê-xu đã từ Giu-đê trở về Ga-li-lê. Vì vậy, ông đến gặp Đức Giê-xu và van xin {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} xuống Ca-bê-na-um chữa cho con trai mình được lành. Con trai ông sắp chết.

ko.L: 이 사람은 예수께서 유대에서 갈릴리로 오셨다는 것을 듣고, 그분께 가서, 내려오셔서 자기 아들을 고쳐 주시기를 청하였다. 아들이 거의 죽게 되었기 때문이다.
ko.B: 그는 예수께서 유대에서 갈릴리로 오셨다는 소식을 듣고 예수께 가서, 내려오셔서 아들을 고쳐 주시기를 거듭 간청했다. 아들이 죽어 가고 있었기 때문이다.
ko.R: 그는 예수께서 유대에서 갈릴리로 돌아오셨다는 말을 들었다. 그래서 예수께 가서, 가버나움으로 내려오셔서 아들을 낫게 해 달라고 간청했다. 그의 아들은 곧 죽을 것 같았다.

pt.L: Este, tendo ouvido que Jesus tinha vindo da Judeia para a Galileia, foi até {{deity_pronoun:ele|Ele}} e {{deity_pronoun:lhe|Lhe}} pedia que descesse e curasse o seu filho, pois estava para morrer.
pt.B: Ao ouvir que Jesus tinha chegado da Judeia à Galileia, foi procurá-{{deity_pronoun:lo|Lo}} e {{deity_pronoun:lhe|Lhe}} suplicava sem parar que descesse e curasse o seu filho, pois o menino estava morrendo.
pt.R: Ele ouviu dizer que Jesus tinha voltado da Judeia para a Galileia. Então foi até Jesus e implorou que {{deity_pronoun:ele|Ele}} descesse até Cafarnaum e curasse o seu filho. O filho dele estava quase morrendo.

am.L: ይህ [ሰው] ኢየሱስ ከይሁዳ ወደ ገሊላ እንደ መጣ ሰምቶ ወደ እርሱ ሄደ፤ ወርዶም ልጁን እንዲፈውስለት ይለምነው ነበር፤ ሊሞት ተቃርቦ ነበርና።
am.B: ኢየሱስ ከይሁዳ ወደ ገሊላ እንደ መጣ በሰማ ጊዜ ወደ እርሱ ሄደ፤ ወርዶ ልጁን እንዲፈውስለትም አጥብቆ ለመነው፤ ልጁ ሊሞት ተቃርቦ ነበርና።
am.R: ኢየሱስ ከይሁዳ ወደ ገሊላ እንደ ተመለሰ ሰማ። ስለዚህ ወደ ኢየሱስ ሄዶ ወደ ቅፍርናሆም ወርዶ ልጁን እንዲያድንለት ለመነው። ልጁ ሊሞት ተቃርቦ ነበር።

hi.L: यह सुनकर कि यीशु यहूदिया से गलील में आ गए हैं, वह उनके पास गया और विनती करने लगा कि वे उतरकर उसके पुत्र को चंगा करें, क्योंकि वह मरने पर था।
hi.B: जब उसने सुना कि यीशु यहूदिया से गलील आ गए हैं, तो वह उनके पास गया और गिड़गिड़ाकर विनती करने लगा कि वे नीचे आकर उसके पुत्र को चंगा कर दें, क्योंकि लड़का मरने पर था।
hi.R: उसने सुना कि यीशु यहूदिया से गलील लौट आए हैं। इसलिए वह यीशु के पास गया और उनसे विनती की कि वे कफ़रनहूम आकर उसके बेटे को ठीक कर दें। उसका बेटा मरने ही वाला था।

ru.L: Этот, услышав, что Иисус пришёл из Иудеи в Галилею, пошёл к {{deity_pronoun:нему|Нему}} и просил, чтобы {{deity_pronoun:он|Он}} спустился и исцелил его сына, ведь тот был при смерти.
ru.B: Услышав, что Иисус пришёл из Иудеи в Галилею, он отправился к {{deity_pronoun:нему|Нему}} и стал умолять {{deity_pronoun:его|Его}} спуститься к ним и исцелить его сына, потому что мальчик умирал.
ru.R: Он услышал, что Иисус вернулся из Иудеи в Галилею. Он пошёл к Иисусу и стал умолять {{deity_pronoun:его|Его}} спуститься в Капернаум и вылечить его сына. Его сын был при смерти.

uk.L: Цей, почувши, що Ісус прийшов з Юдеї в Галилею, пішов до {{deity_pronoun:нього|Нього}} і просив, щоб {{deity_pronoun:він|Він}} зійшов і зцілив його сина, бо той мав померти.
uk.B: Почувши, що Ісус прибув з Юдеї до Галилеї, він пішов до {{deity_pronoun:нього|Нього}} і благав {{deity_pronoun:його|Його}} спуститися й зцілити його сина, бо хлопець помирав.
uk.R: Він почув, що Ісус повернувся з Юдеї до Галилеї. Тож він пішов до Ісуса і благав {{deity_pronoun:його|Його}} прийти до Капернаума й вилікувати його сина. Його син був при смерті.

ja.L: この[人]は、イエスがユダヤからガリラヤに来られたと聞いて、[イエスの]もとに行き、下って来て息子を癒やしてくださるようにと願っていた。息子が死にかけていたからである。
ja.B: この人は、イエスがユダヤからガリラヤに戻って来られたと聞き、イエスのもとに行って、下って来て息子を癒やしてくださるようにと、しきりに願った。息子が死にかかっていたのである。
ja.R: この人は、イエスがユダヤからガリラヤに戻って来られたと聞きました。そこでイエスのところへ行き、カファルナウムまで下って来て息子をいやしてくださいと、必死にお願いしました。息子は今にも死にそうだったのです。

id.L: Ketika ia mendengar bahwa Yesus telah datang dari Yudea ke Galilea, ia pergi kepada-{{deity_pronoun:nya|Nya}} dan memohon kepada-{{deity_pronoun:nya|Nya}} supaya {{deity_pronoun:dia|Dia}} datang ke sana dan menyembuhkan anaknya, sebab anaknya itu hampir mati.
id.B: Ketika mendengar bahwa Yesus sudah datang dari Yudea ke Galilea, ia pergi menemui {{deity_pronoun:dia|Dia}} dan terus memohon kepada-{{deity_pronoun:nya|Nya}} supaya {{deity_pronoun:dia|Dia}} datang dan menyembuhkan anaknya, sebab anak itu hampir mati.
id.R: Dia mendengar bahwa Yesus sudah kembali dari Yudea ke Galilea. Jadi ia pergi menemui Yesus dan memohon supaya {{deity_pronoun:dia|Dia}} mau datang ke Kapernaum dan menyembuhkan anaknya. Anaknya itu sudah hampir mati.

decisions.reason: The imperfect shows a request made again and again. The same verb was used of the Samaritans' request in 4:40.

decisions.choice: come down: from the hill country of Cana to the lakeshore
decisions.reason: Capernaum is far lower than Cana, so one goes "down" to it (2:12). The official asks Jesus to come with him; he assumes the healing needs Jesus to be there.

decisions.choice: he was about to die: at the point of death
alternatives: he was going to die someday
decisions.reason: The verb means to be on the verge of something. The boy was dying.
Readable names the place (meaning decision m2).
Shows that the son, not the father, was dying.

source.text: εἶπεν οὖν ὁ Ἰησοῦς πρὸς αὐτόν· Ἐὰν μὴ σημεῖα καὶ τέρατα ἴδητε, οὐ μὴ πιστεύσητε.

records.literal_gloss: Said therefore the Jesus to him, "Unless signs and wonders you see, not not you will believe."

en.L: So Jesus said to him, "Unless you [people] see signs and wonders, you will certainly not believe."
en.B: Jesus answered him, "None of you will believe unless you see signs and wonders."
en.R: Jesus said to the man, "You people will not believe unless you see signs and wonders."

es.L: Entonces Jesús le dijo: «Si no {{plural_you:ven|veis}} señales y prodigios, de ningún modo {{plural_you:creerán|creeréis}}».
es.B: Jesús le respondió: «Ninguno de {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}} creerá si no ve señales y prodigios».
es.R: Jesús le dijo: «{{plural_you:Ustedes no creerán si no ven|Vosotros no creeréis si no veis}} señales y prodigios».

fr.L: Jésus lui dit donc : « Si vous ne voyez pas de signes et de prodiges, vous ne croirez certainement pas. »
fr.B: Jésus lui répondit : « Aucun de vous ne croira sans voir des signes et des prodiges. »
fr.R: Jésus a dit à l’homme : « Vous tous, vous ne croirez pas si vous ne voyez pas de signes et de prodiges. »

sw.L: Basi Yesu akamwambia, "Msipoona ishara na maajabu, hakika hamtaamini."
sw.B: Yesu akamjibu, "Hakuna hata mmoja wenu atakayeamini msipoona ishara na maajabu."
sw.R: Yesu akamwambia yule mtu, "Ninyi watu hamtaamini msipoona ishara na maajabu."

vi.L: Vậy Đức Giê-xu nói với ông: "Nếu các người không thấy dấu lạ và điều kỳ diệu, thì các người chắc chắn không tin."
vi.B: Đức Giê-xu đáp: "Nếu không thấy dấu lạ và điều kỳ diệu, các người sẽ không bao giờ tin."
vi.R: Đức Giê-xu nói với ông ấy: "Các người sẽ không tin nếu không thấy dấu lạ và điều kỳ diệu."

ko.L: 그러므로 예수께서 그에게 말씀하셨다. "너희는 표적과 기사를 보지 않으면 결코 믿지 않을 것이다."
ko.B: 예수께서 그에게 대답하셨다. "너희는 표적과 놀라운 일을 보지 않고는 아무도 믿지 않을 것이다."
ko.R: 예수께서 그 사람에게 말씀하셨다. "너희 사람들은 표적과 놀라운 일을 보지 않으면 믿지 않을 것이다."

pt.L: Então Jesus lhe disse: "Se vocês não virem sinais e prodígios, de modo nenhum crerão."
pt.B: Jesus lhe respondeu: "Vocês não vão crer de jeito nenhum, a não ser que vejam sinais e prodígios."
pt.R: Jesus disse ao homem: "Vocês só vão acreditar se virem sinais e maravilhas."

am.L: ስለዚህ ኢየሱስ፦ «ምልክቶችንና ድንቆችን ካላያችሁ ከቶ አታምኑም» አለው።
am.B: ኢየሱስም፦ «ምልክቶችንና ድንቆችን ካላያችሁ ማናችሁም አታምኑም» አለው።
am.R: ኢየሱስም ሰውየውን፦ «እናንተ ሰዎች ምልክቶችንና ድንቆችን ካላያችሁ አታምኑም» አለው።

hi.L: तब यीशु ने उससे कहा, "जब तक तुम [लोग] चिह्न और अद्भुत काम न देखो, तुम कभी विश्वास नहीं करोगे।"
hi.B: यीशु ने उससे कहा, "जब तक तुम लोग चिह्न और अद्भुत काम न देख लो, तुममें से कोई विश्वास नहीं करेगा।"
hi.R: यीशु ने उस आदमी से कहा, "तुम लोग तब तक विश्वास नहीं करोगे जब तक चिह्न और अद्भुत काम न देख लो।"

ru.L: Тогда сказал ему Иисус: «Если не увидите знамений и чудес, никак не поверите.»
ru.B: Иисус ответил ему: «Никто из вас не поверит, пока не увидит знамений и чудес.»
ru.R: Иисус сказал ему: «Вы, люди, не поверите, пока не увидите знаков и чудес.»

uk.L: Тож Ісус сказав до нього: «Якщо ви не побачите знаків і див, то ніяк не повірите.»
uk.B: Ісус відповів йому: «Ніхто з вас не повірить, якщо не побачить знаків і див.»
uk.R: Ісус сказав чоловікові: «Ви, люди, не повірите, поки не побачите знаків і див.»

ja.L: そこでイエスは彼に言われた。「あなたがたは、しるしと不思議な業を見なければ、決して信じない。」
ja.B: イエスは彼に言われた。「あなたがたは、しるしや不思議な業を見なければ、だれも信じようとしない。」
ja.R: イエスはその人に言われました。「あなたたちは、しるしや不思議なことを見なければ、信じようとしない。」

id.L: Lalu Yesus berkata kepadanya, "Jika kalian tidak melihat tanda-tanda dan keajaiban-keajaiban, kalian sama sekali tidak akan percaya."
id.B: Yesus menjawab dia, "Kalau tidak melihat tanda-tanda dan keajaiban, kalian tidak akan percaya."
id.R: Yesus berkata kepada orang itu, "Kalian tidak akan percaya kalau tidak melihat tanda-tanda dan keajaiban."

decisions.choice: you: plural, spoken to the man but about the people at large
decisions.reason: Jesus speaks to the official, but both verbs are plural. His words take in the Galileans who welcomed him because of what they had seen (4:45), and the official with them.

decisions.choice: signs and wonders: the phrase for the deeds of the exodus
decisions.reason: The pair is used in the Old Testament for what God did in Egypt (Exodus 7:3; Deuteronomy 4:34; 6:22). It appears only here in John. Joined with "wonders", "signs" here means the striking deed itself rather than what it points to.

decisions.choice: a warning against belief that waits for proof
decisions.reason: The double negative (οὐ μὴ) makes the statement strong: without such deeds you will not believe at all. Jesus does not refuse the man; he challenges a belief that depends on seeing (2:23-25; 20:29). The man answers by pleading again, and then believes Jesus's word before he sees anything (4:50).
Shows that "you" is plural (meaning decision m1).
Literal shows the strong double negative (meaning decision m3).

decisions.choice: vous, without [people] (L); Aucun de vous (B); Vous tous (R)
alternatives: [vous tous] at Literal, as the English
decisions.reason: French "vous" shows the plural that English "you" hides (meaning decision m1), and since Jesus says "tu" to the official (4:50), Literal needs no supplied word; Balanced and Readable make it unmistakable.

decisions.choice: msipoona, hamtaamini: the plural is in the verb
decisions.reason: Jesus answers one man but speaks of "you" in the plural. Swahili marks the plural in the verbs (m-, ham-), so Literal needs no bracketed "[people]"; Balanced and Readable spell it out, as the English does.
"dấu lạ" is the book's word for sign; "điều kỳ diệu" for wonders keeps them two words and avoids "phép lạ", which the book never uses for sign.
Jesus speaks to the man but about people at large; Vietnamese shows the plural with "các người", so no supplied word is needed.
"표적과 기사" is the established pairing and Literal keeps it; "기사" is hard for new readers, so Balanced and Readable say "놀라운 일". "기적" is avoided so that it is not confused with "표적".
Korean "너희" is already plural, so Literal needs no bracketed "[people]" to show that Jesus speaks of more than the man.
Portuguese has a distinct plural "vocês", which already shows that Jesus speaks of more people than the official (meaning decision m1); Literal needs no bracket.
"Sinais e prodígios" is the Portuguese pair for the deeds of the exodus (meaning decision m2), as in Matthew 24:24; Readable says "maravilhas", the plainer word. "Milagre" is avoided, as for "sinal".

John's key term "ምልክት" is kept at every level: his word points beyond the deed to who Jesus is, which "ተአምር" (a miracle) does not say. The plural verb "ካላያችሁ" shows without a bracket that Jesus speaks to more than the one man.

Sign is a key term in John, "चिह्न" at every level and never "चमत्कार"; "signs and wonders" keeps the wording of Matthew 24:24 and Mark 13:22. "तुम लोग" shows that the "you" is plural (meaning decision m1).

'Sign' keeps the book-wide words ('знамение', 'знак'); 'чудо' is used only for the second Greek word, 'wonders', so the two stay apart. Russian 'вы' shows that the man is addressed with the people at large (meaning decision).

"Знак" is John's key word and never "чудо"; "диво" renders *teras* (wonder), the second word of the exodus pair, and keeps it apart from "чудеса", used for *dynameis* in the other Gospels. Literal needs no "[people]": the plural "ви" shows it.

decisions.choice: plural "あなたがた" / "あなたたち" to one man, with no bracket
decisions.reason: Jesus speaks to the official but about people at large (meaning decision m1). The Japanese plural pronoun shows this by itself, so Literal needs no supplied word.

decisions.choice: "しるし" and "不思議な業" (L, B), "不思議なこと" (R)
decisions.reason: "しるし" is the John key term, never "奇跡"; the second word names deeds that cause wonder, kept distinct from it.

source.text: λέγει πρὸς αὐτὸν ὁ βασιλικός· Κύριε, κατάβηθι πρὶν ἀποθανεῖν τὸ παιδίον μου.

records.literal_gloss: Says to him the royal official, "Sir, come down before dies the little child of me."

en.L: The royal official says to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, "Sir, come down before my little child dies."
en.B: The official pleaded, "Sir, come down before my little boy dies."
en.R: The official said, "Sir, please come before my child dies!"

es.L: Le dice el funcionario real: «Señor, baja antes de que muera mi niño».
es.B: El funcionario {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} suplicó: «Señor, baja antes de que se muera mi niño».
es.R: El funcionario {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} dijo: «¡Señor, por favor, ven antes de que mi hijo se muera!».

fr.L: L’officier royal {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} dit : « Monsieur, descends avant que mon petit enfant ne meure. »
fr.B: L’officier insista : « Monsieur, descends avant que mon petit garçon ne meure. »
fr.R: L’officier a dit : « Monsieur, viens vite, s’il te plaît, avant que mon enfant meure ! »

sw.L: Yule afisa wa mfalme anamwambia, "Shuka, bwana, kabla mtoto wangu mdogo hajafa."
sw.B: Yule afisa akamsihi, "Shuka, bwana, kabla kijana wangu mdogo hajafa."
sw.R: Yule afisa akasema, "Tafadhali njoo, bwana, kabla mtoto wangu hajafa!"

vi.L: Viên quan của vua nói với {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}: "Thưa ông, xin xuống trước khi đứa con nhỏ của tôi chết."
vi.B: Viên quan nài nỉ: "Thưa ông, xin ông xuống trước khi con trai nhỏ của tôi chết."
vi.R: Viên quan nói: "Thưa ông, xin ông đến ngay kẻo con tôi chết mất!"

ko.L: 왕의 신하가 그분께 말한다. "선생님, 제 아이가 죽기 전에 내려와 주십시오."
ko.B: 그 신하가 간청했다. "선생님, 제 어린 아들이 죽기 전에 내려와 주십시오."
ko.R: 신하가 말했다. "선생님, 제 아이가 죽기 전에 제발 와 주십시오!"

pt.L: O oficial do rei {{deity_pronoun:lhe|Lhe}} diz: "Senhor, desce antes que o meu filhinho morra."
pt.B: O oficial suplicou: "Senhor, desce antes que o meu filhinho morra."
pt.R: O oficial disse: "Senhor, por favor, vem antes que o meu filho morra!"

am.L: ሹሙ፦ «ጌታዬ፣ ትንሹ ልጄ ሳይሞት ውረድ» ይለዋል።
am.B: ሹሙም፦ «ጌታዬ፣ ትንሹ ልጄ ሳይሞት ውረድ» ብሎ ለመነው።
am.R: ሹሙም፦ «ጌታዬ፣ እባክህ ልጄ ሳይሞት ና!» አለ።

hi.L: राजा का अधिकारी उनसे कहता है, "श्रीमान, मेरे बच्चे के मरने से पहले [नीचे] चलिए।"
hi.B: अधिकारी ने गिड़गिड़ाकर कहा, "महोदय, मेरे नन्हे बेटे के मरने से पहले चलिए।"
hi.R: अधिकारी ने कहा, "साहब, कृपया मेरे बच्चे के मरने से पहले चलिए!"

ru.L: Говорит {{deity_pronoun:ему|Ему}} царский чиновник: «Господин, спустись, прежде чем умрёт моё дитя.»
ru.B: Чиновник взмолился: «Господин, спустись, пока мой мальчик не умер!»
ru.R: Чиновник сказал: «Господин, пожалуйста, пойдём, пока мой ребёнок не умер!»

uk.L: Каже до {{deity_pronoun:нього|Нього}} царський урядовець: «Пане, зійди, перш ніж помре моє дитя.»
uk.B: Урядовець благав: «Пане, прийди, поки не помер мій синочок.»
uk.R: Урядовець сказав: «Пане, прошу, прийди, поки моя дитина не померла!»

ja.L: 王の役人は[イエスに]言う。「主よ、わたしの幼子が死なないうちに、下って来てください。」
ja.B: 役人は願った。「先生、どうか、わたしの幼い息子が死なないうちに、下って来てください。」
ja.R: 役人は言いました。「先生、どうか、子どもが死んでしまう前に来てください。」

id.L: Pegawai istana itu berkata kepada-{{deity_pronoun:nya|Nya}}, "Tuan, datanglah sebelum anak saya mati."
id.B: Pegawai istana itu memohon, "Tuan, datanglah sebelum anak saya yang kecil itu mati."
id.R: Pegawai istana itu berkata, "Tuan, tolong datanglah sebelum anak saya meninggal!"

alternatives: Lord, a confession of who Jesus is
decisions.reason: The address is the polite form used to anyone of standing; the Samaritan woman uses it at 4:11, 15 and 19. The official does not yet know who Jesus is; he believes later (4:53). A footnote gives "Lord".

decisions.choice: my little child: a tender word
decisions.reason: The father uses a diminutive, "little child". John calls the boy his son, and the servants call him "the boy" (4:51).
Like Jesus's mother at Cana (2:3-5), the official is not turned away by Jesus's reply; he simply asks again.
Shows the polite address (meaning decision m1).
Readable shows the urgent pleading in the words.
His words are an urgent plea, which the verb shows.
As at 4:11: Spanish "señor" is the polite address and also "Lord" (meaning decision m1). L and B keep "mi niño" for the father's tender word (m2).

The book-wide choice for John: those who do not yet know who Jesus is address him as "Monsieur", the polite French address to a man, and the footnote on meaning decision m1 gives "Seigneur". The official says "tu" to Jesus, as everyone does in this translation; "Monsieur" carries the respect.
He asks for help but does not yet believe in Jesus, so "kyrie" is the polite address to a man, as in docs/john-terms.md.
He does not yet know who Jesus is, so his "kyrie" is the polite "선생님"; the footnote gives "주님". He speaks in 합쇼체.
As with the Samaritan woman (4:11): "Senhor" is the polite address and also the word for the Lord, and the official speaks to Jesus with "tu", as everyone does (style section 4).

The official does not yet know who Jesus is, so he says "ጌታዬ", as the Samaritan woman does (4:11). As the style guide sets, he speaks to Jesus with "አንተ"; a reviewer may prefer "እርስዎ" for a court official pleading with a stranger.
A respectful address from a man who does not yet know who Jesus is (meaning decision m1), as in 4:11 and the rest of John in Hindi; "प्रभु" would put a confession in his mouth.

The book-wide choice for John: a man who does not yet know who Jesus is says 'Sir', here 'Господин'; 'Господи' (Lord) is kept for those who have come to believe. He says 'ты', as the style guide sets for everyone speaking to Jesus.

The John terms: people who do not yet know who Jesus is say "主よ" at Literal, keeping the word, and "先生" at Balanced and Readable, a respectful address that does not yet confess him as Lord (meaning decision m1).
The word is a tender diminutive (meaning decision m2).
m1: the polite address to a man of standing, as in 4:11, so "Tuan". The official speaks as a petitioner and says "saya" (Style, section 5).

source.text: λέγει αὐτῷ ὁ Ἰησοῦς· Πορεύου· ὁ υἱός σου ζῇ.

records.literal_gloss: Says to him the Jesus, "Go; the son of you lives."

en.L: Jesus says to him, "Go; your son lives."
en.B: Jesus told him, "Go. Your son lives."
en.R: Jesus told him, "Go home. Your son is alive and well."

es.L: Jesús le dice: «Ve, tu hijo vive».
es.B: Jesús le dijo: «Vete. Tu hijo vive».
es.R: Jesús le dijo: «Vuelve a casa. Tu hijo está vivo y sano».

fr.L: Jésus lui dit : « Va ; ton fils vit. »
fr.B: Jésus lui dit : « Va. Ton fils vit. »
fr.R: Jésus lui a dit : « Rentre chez toi. Ton fils est vivant et en bonne santé. »

sw.L: Yesu anamwambia, "Nenda; mwanao yu hai."
sw.B: Yesu akamwambia, "Nenda. Mwanao yu hai."
sw.R: Yesu akamwambia, "Nenda nyumbani. Mwana wako yu hai na mzima."

vi.L: Đức Giê-xu nói với ông: "Hãy đi; con trai ông sống."
vi.B: Đức Giê-xu bảo ông: "Ông hãy đi. Con trai ông sống."
vi.R: Đức Giê-xu bảo ông: "Ông hãy về nhà đi. Con trai ông đã khỏe mạnh rồi."

ko.L: 예수께서 그에게 말씀하신다. "가거라. 네 아들이 산다."
ko.B: 예수께서 그에게 말씀하셨다. "가거라. 네 아들은 살았다."
ko.R: 예수께서 그에게 말씀하셨다. "집으로 가거라. 네 아들은 살았다. 이제 괜찮다."

pt.L: Jesus lhe diz: "Vá; o seu filho vive."
pt.B: Jesus lhe disse: "Vá. O seu filho vive."
pt.R: Jesus disse a ele: "Vá para casa. O seu filho está vivo e passa bem."

am.L: ኢየሱስ፦ «ሂድ፤ ልጅህ ሕያው ነው» ይለዋል።
am.B: ኢየሱስም፦ «ሂድ፤ ልጅህ በሕይወት አለ» አለው።
am.R: ኢየሱስም፦ «ወደ ቤትህ ሂድ፤ ልጅህ በሕይወት አለ፤ ደኅና ነው» አለው።

hi.L: यीशु उससे कहते हैं, "जाओ; तुम्हारा पुत्र जीवित है।"
hi.B: यीशु ने उससे कहा, "जाओ। तुम्हारा पुत्र जीवित है।"
hi.R: यीशु ने उससे कहा, "घर जाओ। तुम्हारा बेटा जीवित और भला-चंगा है।"

ru.L: Говорит ему Иисус: «Иди; твой сын жив.»
ru.B: Иисус сказал ему: «Иди. Твой сын жив.»
ru.R: Иисус сказал ему: «Иди домой. Твой сын жив и здоров.»

uk.L: Каже йому Ісус: «Іди; твій син живе.»
uk.B: Ісус сказав йому: «Іди. Твій син живе.»
uk.R: Ісус сказав йому: «Іди додому. Твій син живий і здоровий.»

ja.L: イエスは彼に言われる。「行きなさい。あなたの息子は生きている。」
ja.B: イエスは彼に言われた。「行きなさい。あなたの息子は生きている。」
ja.R: イエスはその人に言われました。「家に帰りなさい。あなたの息子は生きている。もう元気だ。」

id.L: Yesus berkata kepadanya, "Pergilah, anakmu hidup."
id.B: Yesus berkata kepadanya, "Pergilah. Anakmu hidup."
id.R: Yesus berkata kepadanya, "Pulanglah. Anakmu hidup dan sehat."

decisions.choice: lives: will not die, is well again
alternatives: will live (a promise about the future)
decisions.reason: The verb is present: the boy lives now. In Hebrew usage, to "live" after an illness is to recover (2 Kings 1:2; 8:8-10). Verse 53 shows that the healing happened at the moment Jesus spoke.

decisions.choice: possibly an echo of Elijah: "See, your son lives" (1 Kings 17:23)
alternatives: no echo; the words are ordinary
decisions.reason: Elijah gave a widow back her son with almost the same words in the Greek Old Testament. The phrase is ordinary enough to occur without any echo, so the link is uncertain.

decisions.choice: Go: Jesus sends him home without coming
decisions.reason: The official asked Jesus to come down. Jesus does not go; he speaks the word and sends the father on his way.
Readable says what "lives" means here (meaning decision m1). Literal and Balanced keep "lives", which carries the echo (m2) and returns in verses 51 and 53.
Readable says where he is to go.

decisions.choice: está vivo y sano (R); vive (L, B)
decisions.reason: As in English: Readable says what "lives" means here (meaning decision m1); Literal and Balanced keep "vive", which carries the possible echo (m2) and returns in verses 51 and 53.
Keeping the one verb lets the servants' news and the father's memory repeat Jesus's word, as the Greek does. Jesus calls the official "ông", a respectful address to a man of rank.

Said of someone who was dying, Korean "살았다" means "he has been saved, he will live", which is the sense of the Greek present here; "살아 있다" would only say he has not died yet. Literal keeps the present "산다". The same words are used when the servants and the father repeat it (4:51, 4:53).

decisions.choice: ሕያው ነው (lives, L); በሕይወት አለ (is alive, B, R), repeated in verses 51 and 53
decisions.reason: The same verb comes back in the slaves' report and in the father's memory (verses 51, 53), so each level uses one phrase for it each time.
The Greek verb is 'lives'; Russian 'живёт' would mean 'resides', so it says 'жив', the state the verb means here (meaning decision: will not die, is well again).
Readable says what "lives" means here (meaning decision m1) while keeping "生きている", which returns in 4:51 and 4:53.

source.text: ἐπίστευσεν ὁ ἄνθρωπος τῷ λόγῳ ὃν εἶπεν αὐτῷ ὁ Ἰησοῦς καὶ ἐπορεύετο.

records.literal_gloss: Believed the man the word that said to him the Jesus and was going.

en.L: The man believed the word which Jesus said to him, and set out.
en.B: The man believed what Jesus had said to him and started for home.
en.R: The man believed what Jesus told him, and he started back home.

es.L: El hombre creyó la palabra que Jesús le dijo, y se fue.
es.B: El hombre creyó lo que Jesús le había dicho y emprendió el regreso a casa.
es.R: El hombre creyó lo que Jesús le dijo, y se puso en camino a su casa.

fr.L: L’homme crut la parole que Jésus lui avait dite, et il se mit en route.
fr.B: L’homme crut ce que Jésus lui avait dit et reprit le chemin de sa maison.
fr.R: L’homme a cru ce que Jésus lui avait dit, et il est reparti chez lui.

sw.L: Yule mtu aliliamini neno ambalo Yesu alimwambia, akaenda zake.
sw.B: Yule mtu aliamini yale Yesu aliyomwambia, akaanza safari ya kurudi nyumbani.
sw.R: Yule mtu aliamini kile Yesu alichomwambia, akaanza kurudi nyumbani.

vi.L: Người ấy tin lời Đức Giê-xu đã nói với mình và ra đi.
vi.B: Người ấy tin lời Đức Giê-xu đã nói và lên đường về nhà.
vi.R: Ông tin lời Đức Giê-xu nói, và lên đường về nhà.

ko.L: 그 사람은 예수께서 자기에게 하신 말씀을 믿고 길을 떠났다.
ko.B: 그 사람은 예수께서 하신 말씀을 믿고 집으로 길을 떠났다.
ko.R: 그 사람은 예수의 말씀을 믿고 집으로 돌아가기 시작했다.

pt.L: O homem creu na palavra que Jesus lhe disse e se pôs a caminho.
pt.B: O homem creu no que Jesus lhe tinha dito e partiu para casa.
pt.R: O homem acreditou no que Jesus disse e começou a voltar para casa.

am.L: ሰውየውም ኢየሱስ የነገረውን ቃል አመነ፤ ሄደም።
am.B: ሰውየውም ኢየሱስ የነገረውን አምኖ ወደ ቤቱ መሄድ ጀመረ።
am.R: ሰውየውም ኢየሱስ የነገረውን አመነ፤ ወደ ቤቱም መመለስ ጀመረ።

hi.L: उस मनुष्य ने उस वचन पर विश्वास किया जो यीशु ने उससे कहा था, और चल पड़ा।
hi.B: उस आदमी ने यीशु की कही बात पर विश्वास किया और घर की ओर चल पड़ा।
hi.R: उस आदमी ने यीशु की बात पर विश्वास किया और घर लौटने लगा।

ru.L: Поверил человек слову, которое сказал ему Иисус, и пошёл.
ru.B: Человек поверил тому, что сказал ему Иисус, и отправился домой.
ru.R: Человек поверил тому, что сказал ему Иисус, и пошёл обратно домой.

uk.L: Повірив чоловік слову, яке сказав йому Ісус, і пішов.
uk.B: Чоловік повірив тому, що сказав йому Ісус, і вирушив додому.
uk.R: Чоловік повірив тому, що сказав йому Ісус, і пішов назад додому.

ja.L: その人は、イエスが彼に言われたことばを信じて、出かけて行った。
ja.B: その人は、イエスが言われたことばを信じて、帰って行った。
ja.R: その人は、イエスが言われたことを信じて、家に帰って行きました。

id.L: Orang itu percaya kepada perkataan yang dikatakan Yesus kepadanya, lalu ia pergi.
id.B: Orang itu percaya kepada perkataan Yesus, lalu ia berangkat pulang.
id.R: Orang itu percaya kepada apa yang dikatakan Yesus kepadanya, lalu ia pun pulang.

decisions.choice: he believed Jesus's word before seeing anything
decisions.reason: "Believe" with the word as its object means accepting that what Jesus said is true. Jesus had said that people believe only when they see (4:48); this man believes the word alone. When the word proves true, he believes in the fuller sense (4:53).

decisions.choice: was going: was on his way
decisions.reason: The imperfect leaves him on the road, where the servants meet him (4:51).

decisions.choice: started for home / started back home
decisions.reason: Says where he went; Literal "set out" keeps the bare verb.
With the word as its object the verb means accepting that it is true (meaning decision m1), so Spanish says "creer" + object, as in 2:22, not "creer en".

source.text: ἤδη δὲ αὐτοῦ καταβαίνοντος οἱ δοῦλοι αὐτοῦ ὑπήντησαν αὐτῷ λέγοντες ὅτι ὁ παῖς αὐτοῦ ζῇ.

records.literal_gloss: Already now he going down, the slaves of him met him, saying that the boy of him lives.

en.L: And while he was already going down, his slaves met him, saying that his boy lives.
en.B: While he was still on the way down, his servants met him with the news that his boy was alive.
en.R: While he was still on his way home, his servants came to meet him. They told him, "Your son is alive and well!"

es.L: Y cuando ya bajaba, sus esclavos le salieron al encuentro, diciendo que su muchacho vivía.
es.B: Cuando todavía iba bajando, sus siervos le salieron al encuentro con la noticia de que el muchacho vivía.
es.R: Cuando todavía iba de camino a casa, sus siervos salieron a encontrarlo. Le dijeron: «¡Tu hijo está vivo y sano!».

fr.L: Et comme il descendait déjà, ses esclaves vinrent à sa rencontre, disant que son garçon vit.
fr.B: Il était encore en chemin quand ses serviteurs vinrent à sa rencontre et lui annoncèrent que son garçon vivait.
fr.R: Pendant qu’il rentrait chez lui, ses serviteurs sont venus à sa rencontre. Ils lui ont dit : « Ton fils est vivant et en bonne santé ! »

sw.L: Na alipokuwa akishuka, watumwa wake walikutana naye, wakisema kwamba mtoto wake yu hai.
sw.B: Alipokuwa bado njiani akishuka, watumishi wake walikutana naye na habari kwamba mtoto wake yu hai.
sw.R: Alipokuwa bado njiani kurudi nyumbani, watumishi wake walikuja kumlaki. Wakamwambia, "Mwana wako yu hai na mzima!"

vi.L: Ngay khi ông đang đi xuống, các nô lệ của ông ra đón ông, nói rằng đứa trẻ của ông sống.
vi.B: Khi ông còn đang trên đường xuống, các đầy tớ của ông ra đón và báo tin con trai ông sống.
vi.R: Khi ông còn đang trên đường về nhà, các đầy tớ ra đón ông. Họ báo với ông: "Con trai ông đã khỏe mạnh rồi!"

ko.L: 그런데 그가 벌써 내려가고 있을 때 그의 종들이 그를 맞으며, 그의 아이가 산다고 말하였다.
ko.B: 그가 아직 내려가는 길에 있을 때, 종들이 마중 나와서 아이가 살았다고 알렸다.
ko.R: 그가 아직 집으로 가는 길에 있을 때, 종들이 그를 맞으러 나왔다. 그들이 말했다. "아드님이 살았습니다! 이제 괜찮습니다!"

pt.L: E, estando ele já descendo, os seus escravos foram ao encontro dele, dizendo que o menino dele vive.
pt.B: Quando ainda estava descendo pelo caminho, os seus servos vieram ao encontro dele com a notícia de que o menino estava vivo.
pt.R: Ele ainda estava no caminho de casa quando os seus servos vieram encontrá-lo. Eles disseram: "O filho do senhor está vivo e passa bem!"

am.L: እርሱም ገና በመውረድ ላይ ሳለ ባሪያዎቹ ተቀበሉት፤ ብላቴናውም ሕያው እንደ ሆነ ይነግሩት ነበር።
am.B: ገና በመንገድ ላይ ሳለ ባሪያዎቹ ተቀብለው ልጁ በሕይወት እንዳለ ነገሩት።
am.R: ገና ወደ ቤቱ ሲሄድ ባሪያዎቹ ሊቀበሉት መጡ። እነርሱም፦ «ልጅህ በሕይወት አለ፤ ደኅና ነው!» አሉት።

hi.L: और जब वह अभी उतर ही रहा था, उसके दास उससे आ मिले और कहने लगे कि उसका लड़का जीवित है।
hi.B: वह अभी रास्ते में ही था कि उसके दास उससे मिले और उसे ख़बर दी कि उसका लड़का जीवित है।
hi.R: वह अभी घर के रास्ते में ही था कि उसके दास उससे मिलने आए। उन्होंने उससे कहा, "आपका बेटा जीवित और भला-चंगा है!"

ru.L: Когда же он уже спускался, его рабы встретили его, говоря, что его мальчик жив.
ru.B: Он был ещё в пути, когда его рабы встретили его с вестью, что его мальчик жив.
ru.R: Он ещё не дошёл до дома, когда навстречу ему вышли его рабы. Они сказали ему: «Твой сын жив и здоров!»

uk.L: А коли він уже спускався, його раби зустріли його, кажучи, що його хлопець живе.
uk.B: Коли він був ще в дорозі, його раби зустріли його звісткою, що його хлопець живий.
uk.R: Коли він був ще в дорозі додому, його раби вийшли йому назустріч. Вони сказали йому: «Твій син живий і здоровий!»

ja.L: そして、彼がもう下って行く途中で、彼の奴隷たちが彼を出迎えて、彼の子は生きていると言った。
ja.B: 下って行く途中で、しもべたちが迎えに来て、その子が生きていると告げた。
ja.R: 家に帰る途中、しもべたちが迎えに来ました。そして、「息子さんは生きていて、もう元気です」と言いました。

id.L: Ketika ia sedang dalam perjalanan pulang, budak-budaknya datang menemuinya dan berkata bahwa anaknya hidup.
id.B: Ketika ia masih dalam perjalanan, hamba-hambanya datang menemuinya dengan kabar bahwa anaknya hidup.
id.R: Ketika ia masih dalam perjalanan pulang, hamba-hambanya datang menemuinya. Mereka berkata, "Anak Tuan hidup dan sehat!"

decisions.choice: household slaves, owned by the official
decisions.reason: δοῦλοι were slaves belonging to the household, not hired staff. A royal official would have had several. They come out to give the news.
The word can mean a boy or a servant; here it is the son of verse 46, as "his son" in verse 53 shows.
The servants' news repeats Jesus's word "lives" (4:50), and verse 53 repeats it again. John uses the repetition to show that the word came true.
"Servant" in Balanced and Readable, as the style guide has it; the meaning decision (m1) keeps that the person was owned, and Literal keeps "slave".

decisions.choice: direct speech: "Your son is alive and well!"
decisions.reason: Readable gives their words as they spoke them, which is easier to follow, and uses the same words as verse 50.
As in English: "siervos" in Balanced and Readable, "esclavos" in Literal; meaning decision m1 keeps that they were owned by the household.

French reported speech would normally move the verb into the past ("vivait"), as Balanced does; Literal keeps the present so that the servants' word is heard as the word Jesus used in 4:50 (meaning decision m3).
As in English: "watumishi" (servants) in Balanced and Readable, "watumwa" (slaves) in Literal; meaning decision m1 keeps that they were owned by the official.
The style guide's book-wide choice for doulos, as in the English: Literal names the status, the other levels the household role.
The guide uses "종" for doulos at every level; it covers household servants who were owned, without making slavery itself the point. The English Balanced and Readable say "servants".
Servants speaking to their master say "o senhor" (style section 4); "você" would sound rude from them.

alternatives: አገልጋዮቹ (his servants), as the English Balanced and Readable say
decisions.reason: The style guide keeps "ባሪያ" for this Greek word at every level. Household slaves of a royal official are meant (meaning decision m1), and "አገልጋይ" would hide that they were owned.

The style guide keeps "दास" for this Greek word at every level (section 7b), where the English Balanced and Readable say "servants"; meaning decision m1 notes that they were owned. They say "आप" to their master.
The convention settled in Matthew: doulos is 'раб' at every level; these were household slaves owned by the official (meaning decision).
The Ukrainian brief renders *doulos* "раб" at every level, and the meaning decision says these were household slaves owned by the official; the English Balanced and Readable say "servants".
m1: household slaves. The brief's rule for doulos (Style, section 7): "budak" at Literal, "hamba" at Balanced and Readable.

source.text: ἐπύθετο οὖν τὴν ὥραν παρ’ αὐτῶν ἐν ᾗ κομψότερον ἔσχεν· εἶπαν οὖν αὐτῷ ὅτι Ἐχθὲς ὥραν ἑβδόμην ἀφῆκεν αὐτὸν ὁ πυρετός.

records.literal_gloss: He inquired therefore the hour from them in which better he had; they said therefore to him that, "Yesterday [at the] hour seventh left him the fever."

en.L: So he asked them the hour in which he had gotten better; so they said to him, "Yesterday at [the] seventh hour the fever left him."
en.B: So he asked them at what time the boy had begun to recover, and they told him, "The fever left him yesterday at about one in the afternoon."
en.R: He asked them when his son had started to get better. They said, "Yesterday, at about one o'clock in the afternoon, the fever went away."

es.L: Les preguntó, pues, la hora en que había empezado a mejorar; y le dijeron: «Ayer a la hora séptima lo dejó la fiebre».
es.B: Entonces les preguntó a qué hora había empezado el muchacho a mejorar, y le dijeron: «Ayer, como a la una de la tarde, se le quitó la fiebre».
es.R: Les preguntó cuándo había empezado a mejorar su hijo. Le dijeron: «Ayer, como a la una de la tarde, se le fue la fiebre».

fr.L: Il leur demanda donc l’heure à laquelle il s’était trouvé mieux ; ils lui dirent donc : « Hier, à la septième heure, la fièvre l’a quitté. »
fr.B: Il leur demanda donc à quelle heure l’enfant avait commencé à aller mieux, et ils lui répondirent : « La fièvre l’a quitté hier, vers treize heures. »
fr.R: Il leur a demandé à quel moment son fils avait commencé à aller mieux. Ils ont répondu : « Hier, vers une heure de l’après-midi, la fièvre est partie. »

sw.L: Basi akawauliza saa ambayo alianza kupata nafuu; wakamwambia, "Jana saa saba homa ilimwacha."
sw.B: Basi akawauliza ni saa ngapi mtoto alianza kupata nafuu, nao wakamwambia, "Homa ilimwacha jana yapata saa saba mchana."
sw.R: Akawauliza mwanawe alianza kupata nafuu lini. Wakasema, "Jana, kama saa saba mchana, homa iliondoka."

vi.L: Vậy ông hỏi họ giờ nào nó đã đỡ hơn; họ nói với ông: "Hôm qua, vào giờ thứ bảy, cơn sốt đã rời khỏi nó."
vi.B: Ông hỏi họ đứa bé bắt đầu khỏe lại vào lúc nào, và họ thưa với ông: "Cơn sốt dứt vào khoảng một giờ chiều hôm qua."
vi.R: Ông hỏi họ con trai ông bắt đầu khỏe lại lúc nào. Họ nói: "Hôm qua, khoảng một giờ chiều, cơn sốt đã hết."

ko.L: 그래서 그가 그들에게 아이가 나아지기 시작한 시각을 물었다. 그러자 그들이 그에게 말했다. "어제 일곱째 시에 열이 그에게서 떠났습니다."
ko.B: 그래서 그가 아이가 언제부터 나아지기 시작했는지 묻자, 그들이 대답했다. "어제 오후 한 시쯤에 열이 내렸습니다."
ko.R: 그는 아들이 언제부터 좋아지기 시작했는지 물었다. 종들이 말했다. "어제 오후 한 시쯤에 열이 떨어졌습니다."

pt.L: Então ele lhes perguntou a hora em que ele tinha começado a melhorar; e eles lhe disseram: "Ontem, na hora sétima, a febre o deixou."
pt.B: Então ele lhes perguntou a que horas o menino tinha começado a melhorar, e eles lhe disseram: "A febre o deixou ontem, por volta de uma hora da tarde."
pt.R: Ele perguntou quando o filho tinha começado a melhorar. Eles disseram: "Ontem, por volta de uma hora da tarde, a febre passou."

am.L: ስለዚህ የተሻለው በየትኛው ሰዓት እንደ ሆነ ጠየቃቸው፤ እነርሱም፦ «ትናንት በሰባተኛው ሰዓት ትኩሳቱ ለቀቀው» አሉት።
am.B: እርሱም ልጁ መሻል የጀመረው በስንት ሰዓት እንደ ሆነ ጠየቃቸው፤ እነርሱም፦ «ትናንት ከቀኑ ሰባት ሰዓት ገደማ ትኩሳቱ ለቀቀው» አሉት።
am.R: ልጁ መሻል የጀመረው መቼ እንደ ሆነ ጠየቃቸው። እነርሱም፦ «ትናንት ከቀኑ ሰባት ሰዓት ገደማ ትኩሳቱ ለቀቀው» አሉ።

hi.L: तब उसने उनसे पूछा कि किस समय से वह अच्छा होने लगा; उन्होंने उससे कहा, "कल सातवें घंटे में उसका बुख़ार उतर गया।"
hi.B: तब उसने उनसे पूछा कि लड़का किस समय से ठीक होने लगा था। उन्होंने उससे कहा, "कल दोपहर के लगभग एक बजे उसका बुख़ार उतर गया।"
hi.R: उसने उनसे पूछा कि उसका बेटा किस समय ठीक होने लगा। उन्होंने कहा, "कल दोपहर लगभग एक बजे उसका बुख़ार उतर गया।"

ru.L: Тогда он спросил у них час, в который ему стало лучше; они же сказали ему: «Вчера в седьмом часу его оставила горячка.»
ru.B: Он спросил их, в котором часу мальчику стало лучше, и они сказали ему: «Жар оставил его вчера около часа дня.»
ru.R: Он спросил их, когда его сыну стало лучше. Они ответили: «Вчера около часа дня жар прошёл.»

uk.L: Тож він випитував у них годину, о котрій йому стало краще; і сказали йому: «Учора о сьомій годині гарячка залишила його.»
uk.B: Тож він запитав їх, о котрій годині хлопцеві стало легше, і вони сказали йому: «Гарячка минула вчора близько першої години дня.»
uk.R: Він запитав їх, коли його синові стало краще. Вони сказали: «Учора, близько першої години дня, гарячка минула.»

ja.L: そこで彼は、[その子が]良くなった時刻を彼らに尋ねた。すると彼らは彼に言った。「昨日の第七の時に、熱がその子から引きました。」
ja.B: そこで、子どもが快方に向かったのは何時ごろかと尋ねると、しもべたちは答えた。「昨日の午後一時ごろ、熱が下がりました。」
ja.R: その人は、息子が良くなり始めたのはいつかと聞きました。しもべたちは言いました。「昨日の午後一時ごろ、熱が下がったのです。」

id.L: Lalu ia bertanya kepada mereka pada jam berapa anak itu mulai membaik; dan mereka berkata kepadanya, "Kemarin pada jam ketujuh demamnya hilang."
id.B: Dia bertanya kepada mereka pukul berapa anak itu mulai sembuh, dan mereka menjawab, "Kemarin, kira-kira pukul satu siang, demamnya hilang."
id.R: Dia bertanya kepada mereka kapan anaknya mulai sembuh. Mereka berkata, "Kemarin, kira-kira pukul satu siang, demamnya hilang."

alignments.target_span: at about one in the afternoon

decisions.choice: he had begun to get better
decisions.reason: The phrase means to be better, to be on the mend. The father asks when the improvement began; the servants answer that the fever left him altogether.

decisions.choice: the seventh hour: about one in the afternoon
alternatives: about seven in the morning, counting from midnight
decisions.reason: Hours were counted from sunrise, about six in the morning, so the seventh hour was about one in the afternoon (see 1:39; 11:9). Some have argued that John counts from midnight, which would make it seven in the morning. A footnote gives the literal wording and the other way of counting.

decisions.choice: yesterday: the father reached home the next day
decisions.reason: The journey down to Capernaum was long, so the father met his servants the following day. A Jewish day began at sunset, so if they met after nightfall, the afternoon before was already "yesterday" even if he had traveled only a few hours.
The book-wide choice for John: Literal keeps the clock time, and Balanced and Readable give the modern time (meaning decision m2).
Shows who got better.

decisions.choice: como a la una de la tarde
decisions.reason: The book-wide choice for John: Literal keeps the clock time, and Balanced and Readable give the modern time (meaning decision m2).

decisions.choice: vers treize heures (B); vers une heure de l’après-midi (R)
decisions.reason: The book-wide choice for clock times in John: Literal keeps the Greek count of hours, and Balanced and Readable give the modern time (meaning decision m2). Balanced uses the twenty-four-hour clock usual in written French, as "vers seize heures" at 1:39; Readable says it as people speak.

decisions.choice: saa saba at every level; mchana added at Balanced and Readable
decisions.reason: The seventh hour from sunrise is "saa saba" in Swahili time, about one in the afternoon, so the literal words are also the modern time, as in 1:39 and 4:6.

decisions.choice: በሰባተኛው ሰዓት (L); ከቀኑ ሰባት ሰዓት ገደማ (B, R)
alternatives: the Western clock time, about one in the afternoon
decisions.reason: Ethiopians count the hours from dawn, as the Greek does, so "ከቀኑ ሰባት ሰዓት" names the same time, about one in the afternoon. Literal keeps the Greek ordinal.

decisions.choice: "सातवें घंटे" (L); "दोपहर के लगभग एक बजे" (B, R)
decisions.reason: Clock time: Literal keeps the Greek count; Balanced and Readable give the modern time (style guide section 5; meaning decision m2). "समय" stands for the ordinary hour in 4:52-53; "घड़ी" is kept for Jesus's appointed hour.
The style guide's choice for clock time: Literal keeps the Greek count; Balanced and Readable give the time as a modern reader counts it.

decisions.choice: "о сьомій годині" (L); "близько першої години дня" (B, R)
decisions.reason: Clock times: Literal keeps the Greek count of hours from sunrise; Balanced and Readable give the time as a modern reader counts it (meaning decision).

decisions.choice: "第七の時" (L); "午後一時ごろ" (B, R)
decisions.reason: The John terms: Literal keeps the Greek count of hours from sunrise; Balanced and Readable give the time as a modern reader counts it (meaning decision m2).

decisions.choice: polite speech ("引きました", "下がりました") from the servants to their master
decisions.reason: Household servants speak to the official politely.

source.text: ἔγνω οὖν ὁ πατὴρ ὅτι ἐκείνῃ τῇ ὥρᾳ ἐν ᾗ εἶπεν αὐτῷ ὁ Ἰησοῦς· Ὁ υἱός σου ζῇ, καὶ ἐπίστευσεν αὐτὸς καὶ ἡ οἰκία αὐτοῦ ὅλη.

records.literal_gloss: Knew therefore the father that [it was] in that the hour in which said to him the Jesus, "The son of you lives," and believed he himself and the household of him whole.

en.L: So the father knew that [it was] at that hour in which Jesus said to him, "Your son lives," and he himself believed, and his whole household.
en.B: Then the father realized that it had happened at the very hour Jesus had said to him, "Your son lives." So he came to believe, together with all his household.
en.R: Then the father realized that this was the exact time when Jesus had said to him, "Your son is alive and well." So he and everyone in his home believed in {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.

es.L: Conoció entonces el padre que [fue] a aquella hora en que Jesús le dijo: «Tu hijo vive»; y creyó él y toda su casa.
es.B: El padre se dio cuenta de que había sido a la misma hora en que Jesús le había dicho: «Tu hijo vive». Y creyeron él y todos los de su casa.
es.R: Entonces el padre se dio cuenta de que fue justo a la hora en que Jesús le había dicho: «Tu hijo está vivo y sano». Así que él y todos los de su casa creyeron en {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}}.

fr.L: Le père reconnut donc que [c’était] à cette heure même où Jésus lui avait dit : « Ton fils vit » ; et il crut, lui et toute sa maison.
fr.B: Le père comprit alors que c’était arrivé à l’heure même où Jésus lui avait dit : « Ton fils vit. » Et il crut, avec toute sa maisonnée.
fr.R: Le père a compris que c’était le moment exact où Jésus lui avait dit : « Ton fils est vivant et en bonne santé. » Alors lui et tous les gens de sa maison ont cru en {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}}.

sw.L: Basi baba yake akajua kwamba [ilikuwa] saa ile ile ambayo Yesu alimwambia, "Mwanao yu hai," naye mwenyewe akaamini, pamoja na nyumba yake yote.
sw.B: Ndipo baba yake alipotambua kwamba ilitokea saa ile ile ambayo Yesu alikuwa amemwambia, "Mwanao yu hai." Basi akaamini, yeye pamoja na watu wote wa nyumbani mwake.
sw.R: Ndipo baba yake alipotambua kwamba huo ndio wakati hasa ambao Yesu alimwambia, "Mwana wako yu hai na mzima." Basi yeye na kila mtu wa nyumbani mwake walimwamini Yesu.

vi.L: Vậy người cha biết rằng [đó là] vào chính giờ Đức Giê-xu đã nói với mình: "Con trai ông sống," và chính ông cùng cả nhà ông đã tin.
vi.B: Bấy giờ người cha nhận ra rằng điều ấy đã xảy ra đúng vào giờ Đức Giê-xu nói với ông: "Con trai ông sống." Vậy ông tin, cùng với cả nhà mình.
vi.R: Người cha nhận ra rằng đó chính là lúc Đức Giê-xu đã nói với ông: "Con trai ông đã khỏe mạnh rồi." Vậy ông và mọi người trong nhà đều tin vào {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}.

ko.L: 그러자 아버지는 [그때가] 예수께서 그에게 "네 아들이 산다" 하고 말씀하신 바로 그 시각이었음을 알았다. 그리고 그 자신과 그의 온 집안이 믿었다.
ko.B: 그제야 아버지는 그때가 바로 예수께서 "네 아들은 살았다" 하고 말씀하신 그 시각이었음을 깨달았다. 그래서 그와 그의 온 집안이 믿게 되었다.
ko.R: 그때 아버지는, 그것이 바로 예수께서 "네 아들은 살았다. 이제 괜찮다" 하고 말씀하신 그 시간이었다는 것을 알았다. 그래서 그와 그의 집안 사람들이 모두 예수를 믿었다.

pt.L: Então o pai soube que [foi] naquela hora em que Jesus lhe disse: "O seu filho vive"; e creu ele mesmo e toda a sua casa.
pt.B: Então o pai percebeu que isso tinha acontecido exatamente na hora em que Jesus lhe tinha dito: "O seu filho vive." E ele passou a crer, junto com todos os da sua casa.
pt.R: Então o pai percebeu que tinha sido exatamente na hora em que Jesus tinha dito a ele: "O seu filho está vivo e passa bem." Então ele e todos os da sua casa acreditaram {{deity_pronoun:nele|Nele}}.

am.L: ስለዚህ አባቱ ኢየሱስ፦ «ልጅህ ሕያው ነው» ባለው በዚያ ሰዓት እንደ ሆነ አወቀ፤ እርሱ ራሱና ቤተሰቡ ሁሉ አመኑ።
am.B: አባትየውም ኢየሱስ፦ «ልጅህ በሕይወት አለ» ባለው በዚያው ሰዓት መሆኑን ተረዳ። ስለዚህ እርሱና ቤተሰቡ ሁሉ አመኑ።
am.R: አባትየውም ይህ የሆነው ኢየሱስ፦ «ልጅህ በሕይወት አለ፤ ደኅና ነው» ባለው በዚያው ሰዓት መሆኑን ተረዳ። ስለዚህ እርሱና በቤቱ ያሉት ሁሉ በኢየሱስ አመኑ።

hi.L: तब पिता जान गया कि यह उसी समय हुआ था जिस समय यीशु ने उससे कहा था, "तुम्हारा पुत्र जीवित है," और उसने और उसके सारे घराने ने विश्वास किया।
hi.B: तब पिता ने समझ लिया कि यह ठीक उसी समय हुआ था जब यीशु ने उससे कहा था, "तुम्हारा पुत्र जीवित है।" इसलिए उसने और उसके सारे घराने ने विश्वास किया।
hi.R: तब पिता समझ गया कि यह ठीक उसी समय हुआ था जब यीशु ने उससे कहा था, "तुम्हारा बेटा जीवित और भला-चंगा है।" इसलिए उसने और उसके घर के सब लोगों ने यीशु पर विश्वास किया।

ru.L: Тогда понял отец, что [это было] в тот час, в который сказал ему Иисус: «Твой сын жив», и уверовал сам и весь его дом.
ru.B: Тогда отец понял, что это произошло в тот самый час, когда Иисус сказал ему: «Твой сын жив.» И он поверил, а с ним и все его домашние.
ru.R: Тогда отец понял, что это было именно в то время, когда Иисус сказал ему: «Твой сын жив и здоров.» И он, и все в его доме поверили в {{deity_pronoun:него|Него}}.

uk.L: Тож батько зрозумів, що [це було] тієї години, коли Ісус сказав йому: «Твій син живе», і повірив він сам і весь його дім.
uk.B: Тоді батько зрозумів, що це сталося саме тієї години, коли Ісус сказав йому: «Твій син живе.» І він повірив разом з усією своєю родиною.
uk.R: Тоді батько зрозумів, що це був саме той час, коли Ісус сказав йому: «Твій син живий і здоровий.» Тож він і всі в його домі повірили в {{deity_pronoun:нього|Нього}}.

ja.L: そこで父親は、それがちょうど、イエスが彼に「あなたの息子は生きている」と言われたその時刻であったことを知った。そして、彼自身も彼の家の者全員も信じた。
ja.B: 父親は、それがイエスから「あなたの息子は生きている」と言われたのと同じ時刻だったと気づいた。そして、彼も家の者もみな信じた。
ja.R: 父親は、それがちょうど、イエスが「あなたの息子は生きている。もう元気だ」と言われた時刻だったとわかりました。そして、父親も家の人たちもみな、イエスを信じました。

id.L: Lalu sang ayah tahu bahwa [hal itu terjadi] pada jam yang sama ketika Yesus berkata kepadanya, "Anakmu hidup," dan ia sendiri dan seisi rumahnya percaya.
id.B: Lalu ayah itu sadar bahwa hal itu terjadi tepat pada saat Yesus berkata kepadanya, "Anakmu hidup." Jadi ia menjadi percaya, bersama seisi rumahnya.
id.R: Lalu ayah itu sadar bahwa itulah saat Yesus berkata kepadanya, "Anakmu hidup dan sehat." Jadi ia dan seisi rumahnya percaya kepada-{{deity_pronoun:nya|Nya}}.

decisions.choice: he believed: he became a believer in Jesus
alternatives: he believed the word again, as in verse 50
decisions.reason: In verse 50 he believed what Jesus said. Here the verb stands without an object, as in 1:50 and 20:29: he now believes in Jesus himself. The story moves from asking for a sign, to trusting the word, to belief.

decisions.choice: his whole household: family and servants
decisions.reason: A household included the family and its slaves and dependents. In Acts whole households come to believe together (Acts 10:2, 44; 16:15, 31-34; 18:8).

decisions.choice: the father: the official is now named by his relation to the boy
decisions.reason: John calls him a royal official (4:46, 49), then the man (4:50), and now the father. The title gives way to the parent whose son lives.
Readable says whom they believed in (meaning decision m1).
As in verse 50.
A household included family, slaves and dependents (meaning decision m2); "familia" would leave the slaves out.
As in English: Readable says whom they believed in (meaning decision m1).

decisions.choice: toda a sua casa (L); todos os da sua casa (B, R)
decisions.reason: "Os da sua casa" takes in the servants as well as the family (meaning decision m2); "família" would leave them out.

source.text: τοῦτο δὲ πάλιν δεύτερον σημεῖον ἐποίησεν ὁ Ἰησοῦς ἐλθὼν ἐκ τῆς Ἰουδαίας εἰς τὴν Γαλιλαίαν.

records.literal_gloss: This now again second sign did the Jesus having come out of the Judea into the Galilee.

en.L: And this again [was the] second sign [that] Jesus did, having come from Judea into Galilee.
en.B: Jesus did this, {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} second sign, after {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} had come back from Judea to Galilee.
en.R: This was the second sign Jesus did. It happened after {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} came back to Galilee from Judea.

es.L: Y esta, de nuevo, [fue la] segunda señal [que] hizo Jesús, al venir de Judea a Galilea.
es.B: Esta fue la segunda señal que hizo Jesús, después de volver de Judea a Galilea.
es.R: Esta fue la segunda señal que hizo Jesús. Sucedió después de que volvió de Judea a Galilea.

fr.L: Et cela, de nouveau, [fut le] deuxième signe [que] Jésus fit, étant venu de Judée en Galilée.
fr.B: Jésus accomplit là {{deity_pronoun:son|Son}} deuxième signe, après qu’{{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} fut revenu de Judée en Galilée.
fr.R: C’était le deuxième signe que Jésus faisait. Cela s’est passé après qu’{{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} est revenu de Judée en Galilée.

sw.L: Na hii tena [ilikuwa] ishara ya pili [ambayo] Yesu aliifanya, akiwa amekuja kutoka Uyahudi hadi Galilaya.
sw.B: Yesu alifanya ishara hii, ishara {{deity_pronoun:yake|Yake}} ya pili, baada ya kurudi kutoka Uyahudi hadi Galilaya.
sw.R: Hii ilikuwa ishara ya pili aliyoifanya Yesu. Ilitokea baada ya kurudi Galilaya kutoka Uyahudi.

vi.L: Và đây lại [là] dấu lạ thứ hai Đức Giê-xu đã làm, khi từ Giu-đê đến Ga-li-lê.
vi.B: Đó là dấu lạ thứ hai Đức Giê-xu đã làm, sau khi {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} từ Giu-đê trở về Ga-li-lê.
vi.R: Đây là dấu lạ thứ hai Đức Giê-xu đã làm. Việc ấy xảy ra sau khi {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} từ Giu-đê trở về Ga-li-lê.

ko.L: 그리고 이것은 예수께서 유대에서 갈릴리로 오셔서 다시 행하신 두 번째 표적이었다.
ko.B: 이것은 예수께서 유대에서 갈릴리로 돌아오신 뒤에 행하신 두 번째 표적이었다.
ko.R: 이것은 예수께서 행하신 두 번째 표적이었다. 예수께서 유대에서 갈릴리로 돌아오신 뒤에 일어난 일이었다.

pt.L: E este [foi] de novo [o] segundo sinal [que] Jesus fez, tendo vindo da Judeia para a Galileia.
pt.B: Este foi o segundo sinal que Jesus fez, depois que {{deity_pronoun:ele|Ele}} voltou da Judeia para a Galileia.
pt.R: Esse foi o segundo sinal que Jesus fez. Aconteceu depois que {{deity_pronoun:ele|Ele}} voltou da Judeia para a Galileia.

am.L: ይህም ኢየሱስ ከይሁዳ ወደ ገሊላ መጥቶ ደግሞ ያደረገው ሁለተኛው ምልክት ነው።
am.B: ይህ ኢየሱስ ከይሁዳ ወደ ገሊላ ከተመለሰ በኋላ ያደረገው ሁለተኛው ምልክቱ ነው።
am.R: ይህ ኢየሱስ ያደረገው ሁለተኛው ምልክት ነበር። ይህም የሆነው ከይሁዳ ወደ ገሊላ ከተመለሰ በኋላ ነው።

hi.L: और यह दूसरा चिह्न फिर यीशु ने यहूदिया से गलील में आकर किया।
hi.B: यह यीशु का दूसरा चिह्न था, जो उन्होंने यहूदिया से गलील लौटकर दिखाया।
hi.R: यह दूसरा चिह्न था जो यीशु ने दिखाया। यह तब हुआ जब वे यहूदिया से गलील लौट आए थे।

ru.L: Это опять второе знамение совершил Иисус, придя из Иудеи в Галилею.
ru.B: Это было второе знамение, которое Иисус совершил, вернувшись из Иудеи в Галилею.
ru.R: Это был второй знак, который совершил Иисус. Это случилось, когда {{deity_pronoun:он|Он}} вернулся из Иудеи в Галилею.

uk.L: А це знову другий знак, [який] зробив Ісус, прийшовши з Юдеї в Галилею.
uk.B: Це Ісус учинив як свій другий знак, коли повернувся з Юдеї до Галилеї.
uk.R: Це був другий знак, який зробив Ісус. Це сталося після того, як {{deity_pronoun:він|Він}} повернувся з Юдеї до Галилеї.

ja.L: さて、これは、イエスがユダヤからガリラヤに来て行われた、再び二番目のしるしであった。
ja.B: これは、イエスがユダヤからガリラヤに戻って来て行われた、二番目のしるしである。
ja.R: これは、イエスがなさった二つ目のしるしでした。ユダヤからガリラヤに戻って来られたあとのことです。

id.L: Inilah tanda kedua yang dilakukan Yesus setelah {{deity_pronoun:dia|Dia}} datang dari Yudea ke Galilea.
id.B: Itulah tanda kedua yang dilakukan Yesus, setelah {{deity_pronoun:dia|Dia}} kembali dari Yudea ke Galilea.
id.R: Itulah tanda kedua yang dilakukan Yesus. Tanda itu terjadi setelah {{deity_pronoun:dia|Dia}} kembali dari Yudea ke Galilea.

decisions.choice: again a second sign: the second sign, counted from 2:11
alternatives: a second sign done on a second journey from Judea
decisions.reason: "Again" and "second" together stress the count. The first sign was at Cana (2:11); John mentions other signs in Jerusalem (2:23) but does not number them. The count marks the two signs at Cana, which frame the story from 2:1 to 4:54.

decisions.choice: sign: a deed that points to who Jesus is
decisions.reason: Key term in John (2:11). Here the sign shows that Jesus's word gives life, from a distance and at once (compare 5:24-25).

alternatives: this again was the second sign
decisions.reason: "Again" with "second" says the same thing twice (meaning decision m1); Literal keeps it.
As in English: "again" with "second" says the same thing twice (meaning decision m1); Literal keeps it.
The style guide's term for sign: never "phép lạ" (miracle), since John's word points beyond the deed; "dấu chỉ" is closer to "sign" and is left for a reviewer.
The book-wide choice for John's word 'sign': never 'чудо', since the deed points to who Jesus is.
